CD0008 — Flue Gas Plant.question: In relation to oil tanker cargo spaces which one of the following is the best definition of the expression “gas freeing”?
options: To introduce fresh air into a tank
To increase the amount of inert gas in a tank
To remove all gases from a tank
To reduce the oxygen levels in a tank
CD0008 — Flue Gas Plant.answer: To introduce fresh air into a tank

CD0008 — Flue Gas Plant.question: Which one of the following should be done before starting up the flue gas plant?
options: Calibrate the fixed oxygen analyser
Wash the blowers
Close the uptake valves
Turn off the deck seal pump
CD0008 — Flue Gas Plant.answer: Calibrate the fixed oxygen analyser

CD0008 — Flue Gas Plant.question: Which one of the following is likely to occur if the flue gas temperature is too high at the blower outlet?
options: The coating in the blower may be damaged
A fire might be started in the cargo tank
The pressure control valves may stick
The deck seal may empty
CD0008 — Flue Gas Plant.answer: The coating in the blower may be damaged

CD0008 — Flue Gas Plant.question: How often must the scrubber be flushed with water?
options: Every time it is used
Every hour
Once a year/18 months
Daily
CD0008 — Flue Gas Plant.answer: Every time it is used

CD0009 — Fuel Oil System.question: Some diesel engine manufacturers have introduced the use of fuel and water emulsions as part of their exhaust emissions control measures. How do these emulsions help to reduce air pollutants in exhaust gas emissions?
options: They lower the maximum cylinder temperature and reduce NOx levels
The water washes out sulphur and reduces SOx levels
They dissolve the ash components of the fuel and reduce particulate levels
The oxygen in the water improves combustion of carbon and reduces carbon monoxide levels
CD0009 — Fuel Oil System.answer: They lower the maximum cylinder temperature and reduce NOx levels

CD0009 — Fuel Oil System.question: In fuel combustion what is meant by the term “stoichiometric mixture”?
options: A fuel air mixture which has the ideal minimum amount of air required for complete combustion of the fuel
A fuel air mixture which has less than the ideal minimum amount of air required for complete combustion of the fuel
A fuel air mixture which has more than the ideal minimum amount of air required for complete combustion of the fuel
A fuel air mixture that will not burn
CD0009 — Fuel Oil System.answer: A fuel air mixture which has the ideal minimum amount of air required for complete combustion of the fuel

CD0009 — Fuel Oil System.question: Biodiesel is being proposed as an alternative fuel for use in marine diesel engines. Which one of the options best describes biodiesel that can be used in an unmodified diesel engine.?
options: A blend of petroleum based diesel fuel and less than 20% bio fuel.
A pure product of hydrocarbon based oil refining
A pure product from the processing of vegetable crops.
A blend of petroleum based fuel and water.
CD0009 — Fuel Oil System.answer: A blend of petroleum based diesel fuel and less than 20% bio fuel.

CD0009 — Fuel Oil System.question: Dual fuel diesel engines which use gas and fuel oil are used on some ships. Select the option which best describes one of the methods of operation of the fuel systems for these engines
options: Low pressure gas is used as main fuel with fuel oil used to ignite it
High pressure gas is added to the fuel oil and both injected into the cylinder together
Low pressure gas and fuel oil are injected into the cylinder separately
High pressure gas is used as fuel when fuel oil is not available
CD0009 — Fuel Oil System.answer: Low pressure gas is used as main fuel with fuel oil used to ignite it

CD0009 — Fuel Oil System.question: What is the normal source of ignition in most diesel engines?
options: Heat from the compressed air charge in the cylinder
Heat from the fuel
Heat from a glow plug
A spark igniter
CD0009 — Fuel Oil System.answer: Heat from the compressed air charge in the cylinder

CD0009 — Fuel Oil System.question: Which of the following options best describes the term “self ignition temperature”?
options: The minimum temperature at which a combustible mixture of fuel vapour and air will ignite without an external ignition source
The minimum temperature at which a combustible mixture of fuel vapour and air can be ignited with an external ignition source
Another term for the flash point of a fuel
The minimum temperature at which combustion will continue when the source of ignition is removed
CD0009 — Fuel Oil System.answer: The minimum temperature at which a combustible mixture of fuel vapour and air will ignite without an external ignition source

CD0009 — Fuel Oil System.question: Which one of the following elements of diesel engine exhaust emissions are considered as atmospheric pollutants?
options: H₂O
Heat
Nitrogen
Carbon dioxide
CD0009 — Fuel Oil System.answer: Carbon dioxide

CD0009 — Fuel Oil System.question: Under Marpol Annex VI legislation which one of the following best describes the difference between operating an engine inside a SECA compared to one outside a SECA ?
options: Fuel with a lower sulphur content must normally be used in a SECA
Fuel with a higher sulphur content must normally be used in a SECA
Fuel with a lower nitrogen content must normally be used in a SECA
Fuel with a lower viscosity must normally be used in a SECA1
CD0009 — Fuel Oil System.answer: Fuel with a lower sulphur content must normally be used in a SECA

CD0009 — Fuel Oil System.question: Which one of the following options best describes the gas used as a source of fuel on some LNG carriers?
options: It is a low pressure gas, having evaporated from the cargo tanks
It is a high pressure liquid, having been pumped from the cargo tanks
It is a high pressure liquid, and stored in bunker tanks within the cargo area
It is a low pressure liquid, after processing by the reliquefaction plant
CD0009 — Fuel Oil System.answer: It is a low pressure gas, having evaporated from the cargo tanks

CD0009 — Fuel Oil System.question: What are the products from the complete combustion of hydrogen?
options: Water vapour and heat
Carbon dioxide and heat
NOx emissions
SOx emissions
CD0009 — Fuel Oil System.answer: Water vapour and heat

CD0009 — Fuel Oil System.question: The term “atomisation” is often used in relation to diesel engine fuel injection. Which of the following options best defines the term “atomisation”?
options: The break up of a liquid fuel stream into fine droplets
The formation of a combustible fuel air mixture
The mixing of fuel and air in a diesel engine cylinder
The distribution of fuel in a diesel engine cylinder
CD0009 — Fuel Oil System.answer: The break up of a liquid fuel stream into fine droplets

CD0009 — Fuel Oil System.question: Which one of the following best describes the purpose of the spring in a fuel injection valve?
options: To allow adjustment of the valve closing period.
To give positive seating of the valve to prevent back flow of gas from cylinder into the fuel system
To limit the lift of the valve needle
To allow recirculation of fuel through the valve
CD0009 — Fuel Oil System.answer: To give positive seating of the valve to prevent back flow of gas from cylinder into the fuel system

CD0009 — Fuel Oil System.question: Which one of the following best explains why high pressure fuel pipes fitted to many diesel engines are often double skinned?
options: So that any leakage is contained
So that if the inner skin fails operation can continue using the outer skin
To prevent heat loss by insulating the inner skin
To prevent engine room personnel from contacting the hot inner skin
CD0009 — Fuel Oil System.answer: So that any leakage is contained

CD0009 — Fuel Oil System.question: “Turbulence” is the term used to describe the movement of the charge air in a diesel engine cylinder. Which one of the following options best describes a feature which helps in generating turbulence.
options: The geometry of air inlet ports and valves
The combustion chamber volume
The piston crown material
The length of the charge air receiver
CD0009 — Fuel Oil System.answer: The geometry of air inlet ports and valves

CD0009 — Fuel Oil System.question: Which one of the following options is considered to be a product of incomplete combustion of fuel in a diesel engine cylinder?
options: Carbon monoxide
Nitrogen
Carbon dioxide
Water vapour
CD0009 — Fuel Oil System.answer: Carbon monoxide

CD0009 — Fuel Oil System.question: Fuel oil viscosity control is considered necessary for diesel engines operating on heavy fuel oil. Which one of the following best describes the principle of operation of a Viscotherm unit?
options: Measurement of differential pressure in a capillary tube
Measurement of outlet pressure of the unit pump
Measurement of differential pressure between inlet and outlet to the unit
Measurement of the differential temperature across the unit
CD0009 — Fuel Oil System.answer: Measurement of differential pressure in a capillary tube

CD0009 — Fuel Oil System.question: Many diesel engine high pressure fuel pumps have plungers with helical profiles cut into them. How do these helical profile type plungers control the timing and quantity of fuel delivered to the cylinder.
options: The leading edge controls the start of injection and the trailing edge controls the end of injection
The trailing edge controls the start of injection and the leading edge controls the end of injection
The leading edge controls both the start and end of injection
The trailing edge controls both the start and end of injection
CD0009 — Fuel Oil System.answer: The leading edge controls the start of injection and the trailing edge controls the end of injection

CD0009 — Fuel Oil System.question: Fuels are sometimes blended onboard the ship prior to use. Which one of the following best describes why this process carried out?
options: To control the fuel viscosity at the engine inlet
To control the temperature at the engine exhaust
To control the density at the purifier inlet
To control the temperature at the engine inlet
CD0009 — Fuel Oil System.answer: To control the fuel viscosity at the engine inlet

CD0009 — Fuel Oil System.question: Which one of the following problems is most often associated with blended marine fuels?
options: Instability
Low flash point
High viscosity
High density
CD0009 — Fuel Oil System.answer: Instability

CD0009 — Fuel Oil System.question: Why is variable injection timing, VIT, incorporated in some diesel engine fuel systems?
options: To increase thermal efficiency and reduce specific fuel consumption
To reduce the maximum cylinder pressure
To increase the minimum compression pressure
To increase the maximum load of the engine
CD0009 — Fuel Oil System.answer: To increase thermal efficiency and reduce specific fuel consumption

CD0009 — Fuel Oil System.question: Which one of the following best describes why a low pressure alarm is often fitted in the low pressure part of a diesel engine heavy fuel oil system?
options: To minimise the risk of engine fuel starvation
To indicate when distillate fuel has reached the pump supply manifold
To indicate when the level in the fuel oil service tank is low.
To indicate when the service tank valve is not fully open.
CD0009 — Fuel Oil System.answer: To minimise the risk of engine fuel starvation

CD0009 — Fuel Oil System.question: Which one of the following gases would you normally associate with the combustion of hydrocarbon fuel containing sulphur in a diesel engine?
options: Sulphur dioxide, SO2
Sulphur carbide, SC3
Hydrogen sulphide, H2S
Sulphur oxide, SO
CD0009 — Fuel Oil System.answer: Sulphur dioxide, SO2

CD0009 — Fuel Oil System.question: What is the most common method used to allow the position of fuel cams to be individually adjusted on the camshaft?
options: The majority of fuel cams are mounted on hydraulic sleeve couplings
The majority of fuel cams are mounted on splines
The majority of fuel cams are bolted to flanges
The majority of fuel cams are of split design
CD0009 — Fuel Oil System.answer: The majority of fuel cams are mounted on hydraulic sleeve couplings

CD0009 — Fuel Oil System.question: The vessel you are sailing on, which has one settling tank and one service tank in the fuel system, is due to operate in a SECA. When would you need to start to change over to low sulphur fuel if you are currently operating on normal heavy fuel?
options: At the time before entry into the SECA stated in the ship’s fuel changeover procedure
Just as you enter the SECA
In time to consume the contents of the in service system
In time to consume the contents of the service tank and the in service system
CD0009 — Fuel Oil System.answer: At the time before entry into the SECA stated in the ship’s fuel changeover procedure

CD0009 — Fuel Oil System.question: Which one of the following options best describes why incinerators need a fuel oil system?
options: To establish a flame prior to burning waste oil.
To inject fuel into the sludge before they are pumped to the furnace
To soak solid waste material before burning
To allow the incinerator to be operated when there is no waste oil, sludge or waste material.
CD0009 — Fuel Oil System.answer: To establish a flame prior to burning waste oil.

CD0009 — Fuel Oil System.question: Which one of the following statements is true?
options: Marine diesel oil is a mixture of distillate and a small amount of residual or heavy fuel
Marine diesel oil is a mixture of distillate and a large amount of residual or heavy fuel
Marine diesel oil is a residual fuel
Marine diesel oil is a pure distillate fuel
CD0009 — Fuel Oil System.answer: Marine diesel oil is a mixture of distillate and a small amount of residual or heavy fuel

CD0009 — Fuel Oil System.question: Which one of the following problems is likely to occur if the correct procedure for changing over from heavy fuel to distillate fuel prior to stopping a diesel engine is not followed?
options: SECA limits may not be met
Gassing up due to distillate fuel component overheating
Viscosity control may remain in manual mode
The engine may not stop
CD0009 — Fuel Oil System.answer: Gassing up due to distillate fuel component overheating

CD0009 — Fuel Oil System.question: Which one of the following options is an acceptable method of checking the timing of diesel engine high pressure fuel pumps?
options: Spill cut off method
Matching witness marks on pump casing and camshaft cover
Measuring fuel pump discharge pressure
Testing fuel injector lift pressure
CD0009 — Fuel Oil System.answer: Spill cut off method

CD0009 — Fuel Oil System.question: When diesel engines are operated on heavy fuel oil the fuel is heated up to achieve the correct injection viscosity. How is the fuel system prevented from gassing up when operating this way?
options: By maintaining a high enough pressure in the low pressure system to prevent vapour formation
By increasing the viscosity control setting to limit the fuel temperature
By setting a temperature limit of below 100° C
By operating the system with an open vent
CD0009 — Fuel Oil System.answer: By maintaining a high enough pressure in the low pressure system to prevent vapour formation

CD0009 — Fuel Oil System.question: Some diesel engines have fuel injection systems which incorporate pilot injection. What is the main purpose of using pilot injection?
options: To reduce ignition delay
To increase ignition delay
To increase maximum cylinder pressure
To reduce maximum cylinder pressure
CD0009 — Fuel Oil System.answer: To reduce ignition delay

CD0009 — Fuel Oil System.question: Combustion of fuel oil can be considered to be an energy conversion process. Which of the following options best describes the conversion?
options: Chemical to heat energy
Heat to mechanical energy
Chemical to mechanical energy
Heat to chemical energy
CD0009 — Fuel Oil System.answer: Chemical to heat energy

CD0009 — Fuel Oil System.question: Some diesel engines feature a twin injection system designed to improve fuel injection performance.  Select the option which best describes this feature.
options: A constant amount of fuel is injected by the first injector at all loads while the amount through the second one varies
An equal amount of fuel passes through each injector in sequence
An equal amount of fuel passes through each injector in simultaneously
A variable amount of fuel is injected by the first injector while the amount through the second one is constant at all loads
CD0009 — Fuel Oil System.answer: A constant amount of fuel is injected by the first injector at all loads while the amount through the second one varies

CD0009 — Fuel Oil System.question: Which one of the following features would you expect to find with an inline multi cylinder fuel pump block arrangement?
options: A single rack to control all of the fuel pumps simultaneously.
A separate camshaft for each cylinder
High pressure fuel pipes without bends
Positioning on the engine at crankshaft level
CD0009 — Fuel Oil System.answer: A single rack to control all of the fuel pumps simultaneously.

CD0009 — Fuel Oil System.question: Some diesel engines operate on a fuel mixture which is blended onboard. Which one of the following is a means to control the make up of the blended fuel?
options: Preset viscosity and temperature with varying ratio of blend components.
Preset viscosity and temperature with varying pump pressure
Preset temperature and blend component ratio and varying viscosity
Preset viscosity, temperature and blend component ratio
CD0009 — Fuel Oil System.answer: Preset viscosity and temperature with varying ratio of blend components.

CD0009 — Fuel Oil System.question: What is meant by the term direct injection in relation to diesel engine fuel injection systems?
options: A system in which fuel is injected into the combustion chamber
A system in which fuel is injected into a pre-combustion chamber
A system in which fuel is admitted with the inlet air
A system in which fuel is taken straight from the settling tanks to the engine
CD0009 — Fuel Oil System.answer: A system in which fuel is injected into the combustion chamber

CD0009 — Fuel Oil System.question: Some machines use fuel directly to provide the energy required for operation. Which of the following machines would you include in this group?
options: Diesel engine
Electric motor
Air compressor
Steam turbine
CD0009 — Fuel Oil System.answer: Diesel engine

CD0009 — Fuel Oil System.question: Which one of the following options best describes when you would normally expect to find a thermal oil heating unit fitted onboard a ship?
options: When there is only one steam boiler
When the ship has steam propulsion
When the ship operates on heavy fuel but has no steam boiler
When the ship only has 4 stroke diesel engines
CD0009 — Fuel Oil System.answer: When the ship operates on heavy fuel but has no steam boiler

CD0009 — Fuel Oil System.question: Which one of the following options is a requirement of a diesel engine fuel injection pump?
options: Ensure the correct quantity of air admitted
Ensure the correct quantity of fuel injected
Ensure the fuel at the right temperature to ensure combustion
Ensure the fuel is at the viscosity to ensure combustion
CD0009 — Fuel Oil System.answer: Ensure the correct quantity of fuel injected

CD0009 — Fuel Oil System.question: Which one of the following options best describes why recirculation type fuel injectors are sometimes fitted to diesel engines?
options: They allow engine to be run on heavy fuel oil
A separate fuel valve cooling system is not required
Removes the need for the vessel to carry distillate fuel
Removes the need to have viscosity control
CD0009 — Fuel Oil System.answer: A separate fuel valve cooling system is not required

CD0009 — Fuel Oil System.question: Why is the exhaust from an oil fired boiler a suitable source of inert gas to use to inert cargo tanks on an oil tanker?
options: The boiler exhaust normally contains less than 5% oxygen
The boiler exhaust normally contains no oxygen
The boiler exhaust normally contains about 30% oxygen
The boiler exhaust gas is normally clean and contaminant free
CD0009 — Fuel Oil System.answer: The boiler exhaust normally contains less than 5% oxygen

CD0009 — Fuel Oil System.question: Some boiler use rotary cup burners instead of jet nozzle types. Which one of the following options best describes how rotary cup burners differ from jet nozzle types?
options: Rotary cup burners operate on much lower fuel pressures than simple jet nozzle types
Rotary cup burners rely on electrostatic charge for atomisation of the fuelatomization of the fuel.
Rotary cup burners normally use steam atomisation
Rotary cup burners operate with simple on/off control
CD0009 — Fuel Oil System.answer: Rotary cup burners operate on much lower fuel pressures than simple jet nozzle types

CD0009 — Fuel Oil System.question: Which one of the following options best describes how combustion in a boiler furnace is different to that in a diesel engine cylinder?
options: Boiler combustion is a continuous process.
Boiler combustion requires more excess air
Boiler combustion is started from cold using distillate fuel
Boiler combustion is controlled by measuring the exhaust temperature
CD0009 — Fuel Oil System.answer: Boiler combustion is a continuous process.

CD0009 — Fuel Oil System.question: Many boiler burner units include an air register. What is the purpose of an air register?
options: It controls the quantity of combustion air entering the furnace
It controls the direction and movement of the combustion air entering the furnace
It measures the quantity of combustion air entering the furnace
It prevents backflow of exhaust gas from the furnace
CD0009 — Fuel Oil System.answer: It controls the quantity of combustion air entering the furnace

CD0009 — Fuel Oil System.question: Which one of the following boiler operating parameters would normally give automatic shut down of the boiler in event of alarm condition?
options: Flame failure
Exhaust high oxygen level
High fuel temperature
High steam temperature
CD0009 — Fuel Oil System.answer: Flame failure

CD0009 — Fuel Oil System.question: How is the fuel normally ignited during the start up of a ship’s boiler?
options: Using a spark igniter.
Using the hot furnace air.
Using an external flame.
Using hot furnace brickwork.
CD0009 — Fuel Oil System.answer: Using a spark igniter.

CD0009 — Fuel Oil System.question: Some boiler burner units have steam passing through them during operation. What is the main purpose of using steam in a boiler burner unit?
options: To improve fuel atomisation.
To keep the fuel hot.
To keep the burner part clean.
To heat up the combustion air.
CD0009 — Fuel Oil System.answer: To improve fuel atomisation.

CD0009 — Fuel Oil System.question: Most boiler burner units feature a swirl plate and a diffuser. What is the purpose of these two components?
options: To control the combustion air movement and promote mixing with the fuel.
To control the fuel movement and promote mixing with the combustion air.
To control the amount of air entering the furnace.
To drive the rotary cup part of the burner unit.
CD0009 — Fuel Oil System.answer: To control the combustion air movement and promote mixing with the fuel.

CD0009 — Fuel Oil System.question: Which of the following machines would be described as an internal combustion engine?
options: A diesel engine
A steam turbine
An air compressor
A steam boiler
CD0009 — Fuel Oil System.answer: A diesel engine

CD0009 — Fuel Oil System.question: When would an oil fired inert gas generator normally be fitted onboard an oil tanker?
options: When the vessel has no steam boiler.
When the vessel has a steam propulsion plant
When the vessel has diesel propulsion and an auxiliary steam plant.
When the vessel has steam turbine driven generators.
CD0009 — Fuel Oil System.answer: When the vessel has no steam boiler.

CD0009 — Fuel Oil System.question: What is meant by the term common rail system when applied to a diesel engine fuel injection system?
options: A system in which the high pressure pumps deliver into a manifold supplying all of the fuel injectors.
A system in which the high pressure pumps are supplied from a common suction manifold.
A system in which a multi cylinder fuel pump block is used.
A system where all of the fuel pumps are controlled by a single fuel rack.
CD0009 — Fuel Oil System.answer: A system in which the high pressure pumps deliver into a manifold supplying all of the fuel injectors.

CD0009 — Fuel Oil System.question: Which part of a diesel engine fuel cam profile is normally used to control the rate of fuel delivery?
options: The controlled speed section.
The base circle section.
The cam peak section.
The acceleration and deceleration sections.
CD0009 — Fuel Oil System.answer: The controlled speed section.

CD0009 — Fuel Oil System.question: Variable injection timing, VIT, is sometimes used in the control of a diesel engine fuel injection system. How is a high pressure fuel pump using valve control arranged to provide VIT?
options: The governor output is used to control both suction and spill valve.
The governor output is used to control only the suction valve.
The governor output is used to control only the spill valve.
The governor output is used to control only the delivery valve.
CD0009 — Fuel Oil System.answer: The governor output is used to control both suction and spill valve.

CD0009 — Fuel Oil System.question: Some high pressure pumps used in diesel engine fuel injection systems control the timing and quantity with a valve arrangement rather than a helix cut into the plunger. How is control of the pumps usually achieved using valves?
options: Suction valve to control start of injection and spill valve to control the end.
Spill valve to control start of injection and suction valve to control the end.
Suction valve to control the start and end of injection.
Spill valve to control the start and end of injection.
CD0009 — Fuel Oil System.answer: Suction valve to control start of injection and spill valve to control the end.

CD0009 — Fuel Oil System.question: The peak pressure allowed in a diesel engine cylinder is limited to a maximum value during the engine design stage. What determines this limit?
options: The strength of the combustion chamber components.
The amount of fuel that can be injected into the cylinder.
The amount of charge air that can be admitted to the cylinder.
The cylinder compression pressure.
CD0009 — Fuel Oil System.answer: The strength of the combustion chamber components.

CD0009 — Fuel Oil System.question: The term jerk pump is often used when describing the type of high pressure fuel pump used in diesel engine fuel injection systems. Which one of the following options best defines this type of pump?
options: A cam actuated pump which has a rapid movement.
A crank actuated pump delivering to a common manifold.
A distributor type pump driven from the camshaft.
A positive displacement pump.
CD0009 — Fuel Oil System.answer: A cam actuated pump which has a rapid movement.

CD0009 — Fuel Oil System.question: On large diesel engines it is common practice to use individual high pressure pumps positioned at each cylinder unit. Which one of the following gives the reason for doing this?
options: To keep the high pressure fuel pipes as short as possible.
To allow a long camshaft to be used.
To make the pump adjustment easier.
To reduce the size of the pump units.
CD0009 — Fuel Oil System.answer: To keep the high pressure fuel pipes as short as possible.

CD0009 — Fuel Oil System.question: Which of the following fuel components will release the most energy, measured in MJ/kg, during the combustion of marine residual fuel?
options: Hydrogen
Carbon
Ash
Sulphur
CD0009 — Fuel Oil System.answer: Hydrogen

CD0009 — Fuel Oil System.question: The complete combustion of carbon should produce which of the given options?
options: Carbon dioxide and heat
Carbon monoxide and heat
Carbon dioxide, water vapour and heat
NOx and SOx components in the exhaust gas emissions
CD0009 — Fuel Oil System.answer: Carbon dioxide and heat

CD0009 — Fuel Oil System.question: Which one of the following options is the best definition of the “flash point” of a fuel?
options: The temperature at which a fuel gives off vapours which can be ignited by an external ignition source.
The temperature at which a fuel will spontaneously ignite.
The temperature at which the fuel changes state from liquid to gas.
The temperature at which fuel will continue to burn once ignited.
CD0009 — Fuel Oil System.answer: The temperature at which a fuel gives off vapours which can be ignited by an external ignition source.

CD0009 — Fuel Oil System.question: Which one of the following options best describes a “stoichiometric mixture”?
options: A mixture of fuel and air containing the exact theoretical amount of air for complete combustion of the fuel.
A mixture of fuel and air containing approximately 5% excess air.
A mixture of fuel and air containing approximately 30% excess air.
A mixture of fuel and air that will ignite.
CD0009 — Fuel Oil System.answer: A mixture of fuel and air containing the exact theoretical amount of air for complete combustion of the fuel.

CD0009 — Fuel Oil System.question: Which marine legislation has led to the introduction of low sulphur fuels in the shipping industry?
options: Marpol (Annex VI)
The ISM Code.
Marpol (Annex I)
SOLAS
CD0009 — Fuel Oil System.answer: Marpol (Annex VI)

CD0009 — Fuel Oil System.question: Select the correct option from those given to complete the statement. The fuel standard commonly used for the specification of marine fuels is ...
options: ISO 8217
Marpol (Annex I)
SOLAS
ISO 2008
CD0009 — Fuel Oil System.answer: ISO 8217

CD0009 — Fuel Oil System.question: Some diesel engines operate with pilot injection as a feature of the fuel injection system. How is pilot injection usually achieved?
options: By having two injection periods with a single injector.
By having two fuel injection pumps.
By having two fuel cam profiles.
By having two injectors injecting fuel at the same time.
CD0009 — Fuel Oil System.answer: By having two injection periods with a single injector.

CD0009 — Fuel Oil System.question: Water/fuel emulsions are used in some diesel engines as a means of reducing the level of NOx emissions. What is a possible side effect of using these emulsions?
options: Emulsions will give some secondary atomisation of heavy fuel improving combustion efficiency.
Emulsions normally result in lower specific fuel consumption
Emulsions normally assist in lubricating the cylinder liner.
Emulsions normally reduce SOx levels.
CD0009 — Fuel Oil System.answer: Emulsions will give some secondary atomisation of heavy fuel improving combustion efficiency.

CD0010 — Marine fuel handling.question: A purifier is used to clean the fuel prior to delivering it to the service tank for use in the engine. Which one of the options shows what should be removed from the fuel by the purifier?
options: Water and dirt.
Water.
Dirt.
Microbial contamination.
Incorrect.
Correct.
CD0010 — Marine fuel handling.answer: Water and dirt.

CD0010 — Marine fuel handling.question: Stabilisers are sometimes used as part of the fuel treatment to improve performance. Which of the given options best describes the action of fuel stabilisers?
options: They reduce the oxidation rate in storage.
They kill off any microbes in the fuel.
They help to separate out any water from the fuel.
They break up heavy hydrocarbons.
Incorrect.
Correct.
CD0010 — Marine fuel handling.answer: They reduce the oxidation rate in storage.

CD0010 — Marine fuel handling.question: The purpose of the fuel settling tank is to allow water and dirt in the fuel to separate so it can be drained off. Which of the following factors is the main reason for the separation occurring?
options: Difference in density between the fuel and the water and dirt.
Difference in viscosity between the fuel and the water and dirt.
Difference in temperature between the fuel and the water and dirt.
Difference in volume between the fuel and the water and dirt.
Incorrect.
Correct.
CD0010 — Marine fuel handling.answer: Difference in density between the fuel and the water and dirt.

CD0010 — Marine fuel handling.question: A centrifuge is used to give more effective separation of water and dirt from fuel. How does it achieve this better separation?
options: By increasing the separating force by centrifugal action.
By having a self cleaning facility.
By having a high flow rate.
By using gravity discs.
Incorrect.
Correct.
CD0010 — Marine fuel handling.answer: By increasing the separating force by centrifugal action.

CD0010 — Marine fuel handling.question: High density fuels cannot be treated with a conventional purifier to remove water. Which one of the given options is the reason for this?
options: Insufficient density difference between water and fuel.
Insufficient heating facility.
Insufficient flow rates.
Emulsification of fuel and water.
Incorrect.
Correct.
CD0010 — Marine fuel handling.answer: Insufficient density difference between water and fuel.

CD0010 — Marine fuel handling.question: Safe operation and pollution prevention procedures should be contained in the ships Safety Management Manual as part of the company’s Safety Management System. Which legislation requires this?
options: ISM Code
MARPOL
FSS Code
COLREGS
Incorrect.
Correct.
CD0010 — Marine fuel handling.answer: ISM Code

CD0010 — Marine fuel handling.question: MARPOL Annex I deals with the prevention of which of the following forms of marine pollution from ships?
options: Pollution by oil
Pollution by garbage
Pollution by sewage
Pollution by noxious liquid substances in bulk
Incorrect.
Correct.
CD0010 — Marine fuel handling.answer: Pollution by oil

CD0010 — Marine fuel handling.question: MARPOL Annex I requires new ships with a total bunker capacity greater than a certain limit to have fuel oil tanks positioned so that no part of the tank is formed by the outer hull plating. What is the limit?
options: 600 m³
150 m³
Incorrect.
Correct.
CD0010 — Marine fuel handling.answer: 600 m³

CD0010 — Marine fuel handling.question: Which of the following options describes a feature required where sight glasses are used to show fuel oil tank contents?
options: Self closing cocks or valves.
Seamless tubular glass.
Test cocks.
Screw caps.
Incorrect.
Correct.
CD0010 — Marine fuel handling.answer: Self closing cocks or valves.

CD0010 — Marine fuel handling.question: Which one of the following options is a fitting that will always be found on fuel oil service and settling tanks?
options: Self closing drain valve or cock.
Remote reading contents gauge.
Sight glass.
High and low level alarms.
Incorrect.
Correct.
CD0010 — Marine fuel handling.answer: Self closing drain valve or cock.

CD0010 — Marine fuel handling.question: Edge filters are used for removal of very small particles. Which one of the following best describes where you would be likely to find edge filters fitted in the fuel oil system?
options: Before fuel injection equipment.
At the fuel tank outlet connection.
At purifier inlet connections.
Before the viscosity controller.
Incorrect.
Correct.
CD0010 — Marine fuel handling.answer: Before fuel injection equipment.

CD0010 — Marine fuel handling.question: Back flushing filters are sometimes fitted in the onboard fuel oil treatment system. Which one of the following options best describes what the unit is normally back flushed with?
options: Cleaned fuel.
Water.
Air.
Diesel oil.
Incorrect.
Correct.
CD0010 — Marine fuel handling.answer: Cleaned fuel.

CD0010 — Marine fuel handling.question: Which one of the following options must be fitted on an air vent for a fuel oil tank?
options: Flame screen.
Self closing cock.
Filter.
Pressure indicator.
Incorrect.
Correct.
CD0010 — Marine fuel handling.answer: Flame screen.

CD0010 — Marine fuel handling.question: Which one of the fittings listed would you expect to find on a fuel oil tank air vent positioned on an open weather deck?
options: Vent head with float type shut off valve or similar.
Self closing cock.
Test cock.
Remote closing valve.
Incorrect.
Correct.
CD0010 — Marine fuel handling.answer: Vent head with float type shut off valve or similar.

CD0010 — Marine fuel handling.question: The number of fuel oil tanks in a ship is decided upon by considering a number of factors. Which one of the options is one of the most important factors which would be taken into consideration?
options: Cargo carrying capacity.
Segregation of fuel types
Tank vent positions.
Fuel transfer pump capabilities.
Incorrect.
Correct.
CD0010 — Marine fuel handling.answer: Segregation of fuel types

CD0010 — Marine fuel handling.question: Which one of the following would be the normal way to remove microbial contamination from fuel oil?
options: Treatment with biocides.
Treatment with fuel stabilisers.
Treatment with combustion improvers.
Regular draining of tanks.
Incorrect.
Correct.
CD0010 — Marine fuel handling.answer: Treatment with biocides.

CD0010 — Marine fuel handling.question: Some centrifuges used for oil have a solenoid valve in the water outlet which is controlled by a water sensor in the oil outlet. What is this type of centrifuge used for?
options: Treating high density residual fuel oils.
Treating lubricating oil.
Treating distillate fuel oils.
Treating fuels with minimum water content.
Incorrect.
Correct.
CD0010 — Marine fuel handling.answer: Treating high density residual fuel oils.

CD0010 — Marine fuel handling.question: The main purpose of purging cargo tanks with Inert Gas (IG) is to prevent explosive atmosphere in the tanks. What are the standard requirements for oxygen content in the IG supply line and in the cargo tanks?
options: Maximum 5% and 8% respectively
Maximum 6% and 11% respectively
Maximum 0% and 5% respectively
Maximum 2% and 5% respectively
CD0010 — Marine fuel handling.answer: Maximum 5% and 8% respectively

CD0010 — Marine fuel handling.question: Which of the following options would you describe as being a double bottom tank?
options: A tank formed between the hull bottom plating and the inner floor plating.
A tank with a void space in the bottom.
A tank where the hull plating is double thickness.
A tank which can be used for two different purposes.
Incorrect.
Correct.
CD0010 — Marine fuel handling.answer: A tank formed between the hull bottom plating and the inner floor plating.

CD0010 — Marine fuel handling.question: Which one of the following describes the normal way of removing accumulated water from a fuel oil settling tank?
options: Regular draining using the drain cock.
During manual cleaning.
With a water pump.
With a centrifuge.
Incorrect.
Correct.
CD0010 — Marine fuel handling.answer: Regular draining using the drain cock.

CD0010 — Marine fuel handling.question: A fuel oil tank is fitted with a sounding pipe which is used from within the engine room. Which one of the following fittings given must be fitted?
options: Self closing cock with test cock.
Non return float valve.
Flame trap.
Tank high level alarm.
Incorrect.
Correct.
CD0010 — Marine fuel handling.answer: Self closing cock with test cock.

CD0010 — Marine fuel handling.question: When a centrifuge is set up as a fuel oil clarifier it normally only separates solids from the dirty fuel. How is the set up of a clarifier different to that for a purifier?
options: The water outlet is closed off by the top cover of the disc stack.
The water outlet is closed off by a solenoid valve.
The disc stack has no distribution holes.
The gravity discs with the largest diameter holes are fitted.
Incorrect.
Correct.
CD0010 — Marine fuel handling.answer: The water outlet is closed off by the top cover of the disc stack.

CD0010 — Marine fuel handling.question: Which one of the following options best describes the conditions under which microbial contamination of distillate fuel is most likely to occur?
options: Water is present in the fuel.
Oxygen is present in the fuel.
Oxygen is not present in the fuel.
The fuel contains sulphur.
Incorrect.
Correct.
CD0010 — Marine fuel handling.answer: Water is present in the fuel.

CD0010 — Marine fuel handling.question: Filters are often fitted as part of the fuel oil cleaning arrangement. Which one of the following best describes why duplex (double) filter units are normally fitted?
options: To allow cleaning without interrupting the fuel supply.
To double the cleaning effect.
To allow automatic cleaning of the elements.
To have filters with different gauge mesh in operation at the same time.
Incorrect.
Correct.
CD0010 — Marine fuel handling.answer: To allow cleaning without interrupting the fuel supply.

CD0010 — Marine fuel handling.question: Which of the following options best completes the following statement? ^M^MThe main reason for heating fuel oil before it enters a purifier is to …
options: increase the density difference between fuel and water.
increase the viscosity difference between fuel and water.
decrease the density difference between fuel and water.
decrease the viscosity difference between fuel and water.
Incorrect.
Correct.
CD0010 — Marine fuel handling.answer: increase the density difference between fuel and water.

CD0010 — Marine fuel handling.question: When used in relation to fuel oil, the term instability refers to which one of the following situations?
options: Possibility that fuel components will separate during storage.
Possibility that the fuel will burn unevenly during combustion.
Possibility that the fuel will require additional heating for transfer.
The fuel is a blend of two or more grades.
Incorrect.
Correct.
CD0010 — Marine fuel handling.answer: Possibility that fuel components will separate during storage.

CD0010 — Marine fuel handling.question: Which of the following options gives the maximum temperature allowed for the heating medium in a fuel oil tank?
options: 220° Celsius.
150° Celsius.
100° Celsius.
180° Celsius.
Incorrect.
Correct.
CD0010 — Marine fuel handling.answer: 220° Celsius.

CD0010 — Marine fuel handling.question: Fuel oil treatment systems sometimes include ultrasonic devices. Which one of the following best describes how these devices improve the condition of the fuel?
options: They generate high energy vibrations which break down contaminant particles and heavy molecules.
They generate electrical pulses which break down contaminant particles and heavy molecules.
They generate magnetic fields which break down contaminant particles and heavy molecules.
They grind down contaminant particles and heavy molecules.
Incorrect.
Correct.
CD0010 — Marine fuel handling.answer: They generate high energy vibrations which break down contaminant particles and heavy molecules.

CD0010 — Marine fuel handling.question: Mechanical homogenisers are sometimes fitted as part of the fuel oil treatment arrangement. Which one of the following options given best describes the effect of an homogeniser on fuel oil?
options: Grinds solid particles down in size.
Increases the density.
Reduces the density.
Separate solids and water from the fuel.
Incorrect.
Correct.
CD0010 — Marine fuel handling.answer: Grinds solid particles down in size.

CD0010 — Marine fuel handling.question: Chemical additives and stabilisers are sometimes used as part of the fuel oil treatment. Which one of the following best describes how fuel stabilisers are intended to work?
options: Preventing the fuel from ageing.
Forming stable emulsions.
Changing the fuel molecules.
By introducing chemicals which ignite more easily.
Incorrect.
Correct.
CD0010 — Marine fuel handling.answer: Preventing the fuel from ageing.

CD0010 — Marine fuel handling.question: Centrifuges are often used in pairs to give combined cleaning effect on fuel oil. Which of the options given is the preferred arrangement for these combinations?
options: Purifier and clarifier in series.
Two purifiers in parallel.
Two clarifiers in series.
Purifier and clarifier in parallel.
Incorrect.
Correct.
CD0010 — Marine fuel handling.answer: Purifier and clarifier in series.

CD0010 — Marine fuel handling.question: Which one of the following options describes the aim of legislative changes that now require many ships to have fuel oil tanks sited away from the ship’s side and bottom?
options: Reduce pollution in the event of collision or grounding.
Increase the ballast capacity of ships.
Reduce the amount of cargo that can be carried.
Increase the amount of fuel that can be carried.
Incorrect.
Correct.
CD0010 — Marine fuel handling.answer: Reduce pollution in the event of collision or grounding.

CD0010 — Marine fuel handling.question: Which of the following options best describes the term “incompatible” when applied to fuel oil?
options: The fuel become unstable and form sludges when mixed with another fuel.
The components of a fuel separate out over time.
The fuel is not suitable for the machinery onboard.
The fuel does not match the ISO 8217 specification.
Incorrect.
Correct.
CD0010 — Marine fuel handling.answer: The fuel become unstable and form sludges when mixed with another fuel.

CD0010 — Marine fuel handling.question: MARPOL Annex VI deals with the prevention of which one of the following forms of pollution from ships?
options: Air pollution due to exhaust emissions.
Marine pollution by oil.
Environmental pollution by garbage.
Environmental pollution by harmful substances carried in packaged form.
Incorrect.
Correct.
CD0010 — Marine fuel handling.answer: Air pollution due to exhaust emissions.

CD0010 — Marine fuel handling.question: Which one of the following options describes when remote closing valves are required to be fitted in fuel oil tank outlet lines?
options: When the fuel oil tank is in the same space as the machinery it supplies.
Required for all fuel oil tanks.
Only required for fuel oil settling tanks.
Only required for fuel oil service tanks.
Incorrect.
Correct.
CD0010 — Marine fuel handling.answer: When the fuel oil tank is in the same space as the machinery it supplies.

CD0010 — Marine fuel handling.question: Suction strainers are fitted to most fuel oil treatment systems. Which one of the following best describes the main purpose of a suction strainer?
options: To protect the pumps from large solid particles.
To protect the pumps from any water in the fuel.
To remove all of the solids in the fuel.
To improve the flow rate to the centrifuges.
Incorrect.
Correct.
CD0010 — Marine fuel handling.answer: To protect the pumps from large solid particles.

CD0010 — Marine fuel handling.question: Which one of the following best describes how water is removed from fuel oil when static filter modules are used instead of centrifuges?
options: They contain coalescer elements.
They contain paper elements.
They contain fine mesh elements.
They contain edge filter elements.
Incorrect.
Correct.
CD0010 — Marine fuel handling.answer: They contain coalescer elements.

CD0010 — Marine fuel handling.question: When centrifuges are set up as fuel oil purifiers they often have gravity discs or gravity plugs fitted. How does fitting different sizes of these allow fuels of different densities to be treated?
options: They control the position of the interface.
They alter the height of the disc stack.
They alter the position of the oil outlet.
They alter the flow rate through the purifier.
Incorrect.
Correct.
CD0010 — Marine fuel handling.answer: They control the position of the interface.

CD0010 — Marine fuel handling.question: Fuel tank vent pipes positioned on the open deck are normally fitted with an automatic valve. What is the purpose of this valve?
options: To prevent water entering the tank during rough weather.
To prevent fuel oil spilling from the vent pipe.
To prevent air from entering the tank.
To allow vapours to escape from the tank.
Incorrect.
Correct.
CD0010 — Marine fuel handling.answer: To prevent water entering the tank during rough weather.

CD0010 — Marine fuel handling.question: Incompatibility is the term used to describe which one of the fuel oil storage problems given in the answer options?
options: Sludge formation following mixing of two normally stable fuels.
Separation of the heavy and distillate components of a fuel.
Occurrence of microbial contamination of a fuel.
Settling out of dirt from contaminated fuel oil.
Incorrect.
Correct.
CD0010 — Marine fuel handling.answer: Sludge formation following mixing of two normally stable fuels.

CD0010 — Marine fuel handling.question: MARPOL allows fuel oil to be stored within the fore peak and after peak tanks. True or false?
options: False
True
Incorrect.
Correct.
CD0010 — Marine fuel handling.answer: False

CD0010 — Marine fuel handling.question: The International Maritime Organisation’s pollution legislation, Marpol, contains six annexes dealing with different aspects of marine pollution. Which of the options is the MARPOL annex which deals with air pollution by ships?
options: Annex VI
Annex I
Annex III
Annex V
Incorrect.
Correct.
CD0010 — Marine fuel handling.answer: Annex VI

CD0010 — Marine fuel handling.question: The International Safety Management Code, the ISM Code, as it is commonly referred to, deals with which of the given options?
options: The safe operation of ships and the prevention of pollution by ships.
Only the safe operation of ships.
Only the prevention of pollution by ships.
Only environmental safety.
Incorrect.
Correct.
CD0010 — Marine fuel handling.answer: The safe operation of ships and the prevention of pollution by ships.

CD0010 — Marine fuel handling.question: The International Maritime Organisation’s pollution legislation, Marpol, contains six annexes dealing with different aspects of marine pollution. Which of the options is the annex dealing with oil pollution by ships?
options: Annex I
Annex II
Annex III
Annex IV
Incorrect.
Correct.
CD0010 — Marine fuel handling.answer: Annex I

CD0012 — Tanker operation I.question: What is the main reason for crude oil tankers to be fitted with a Vapour Emission Control System or Vapour Return System?
options: Because vapours emitted from crude oil cargo are toxic and can harm human health and the environment.
To prevent loss of cargo through vapour release to the atmosphere.
Collected vapours can be used in the vessel’s boiler so it is a commercial reason.
The vapours are returned back to the shore tank and mixed with the crude oil so it is a commercial reason.
CD0012 — Tanker operation I.answer: Because vapours emitted from crude oil cargo are toxic and can harm human health and the environment.

CD0012 — Tanker operation I.question: Who is responsible for checking  the vessel’s moorings during loading operations?
options: Bosun under the supervision of the duty deck officer.
The 2nd.Officer.
The Ship Security Officer.
Bosun and the pumpman.
CD0012 — Tanker operation I.answer: Bosun under the supervision of the duty deck officer.

CD0012 — Tanker operation I.question: All crude oil tankers are required to have a certain amount of oil pollution prevention equipment on board. Where would details, relating to the specific equipment on your ship, be found?
options: In the Shipboard Oil Pollution Emergency Plan (SOPEP).
In the Company’s Contingency Manual.
In the MARPOL 73/78 Consolidated regulations.
In the International Safety Guide for Oil Tankers and Terminals (ISGOTT).
CD0012 — Tanker operation I.answer: In the Shipboard Oil Pollution Emergency Plan (SOPEP).

CD0012 — Tanker operation I.question: Junior officers are responsible for maintenance of the vessel’s fire fighting and life saving equipment and it is a requirement that completion of these maintenance routines is recorded. Which regulations require these records to be made?
options: The International Convention for the Safety of Life at Sea (SOLAS).
The International Safety Management Code (ISM Code).
The MARPOL Annex I regulations.
The International Safety Guide for Oil Tankers and Terminals (ISGOTT).
CD0012 — Tanker operation I.answer: The International Convention for the Safety of Life at Sea (SOLAS).

CD0012 — Tanker operation I.question: When entering a ballast tank for internal inspection, does it require the same procedures as for a cargo tank with respect to “enclosed space entry”?
options: Yes, all tanks should be considered as enclosed spaces.
No, only cargo tanks are considered as enclosed spaces.
No, ballast tanks are clean and do not require the same precautions to be taken as for cargo tanks.
No, only hard hats and hand torches are required when inspecting ballast tanks.
CD0012 — Tanker operation I.answer: Yes, all tanks should be considered as enclosed spaces.

CD0012 — Tanker operation I.question: On the laden voyage the vessel’s integrity and structural conditions need to be checked and monitored, such as atmosphere in empty spaces, water ingress and leakages. Where should the results of these checks normally be recorded?
options: In the Deck Log Book.
In the vessel’s Planned Maintenance System (PMS).
In the vessel’s Ballast Water Management Plan.
In the vessels tank inspection records.
CD0012 — Tanker operation I.answer: In the Deck Log Book.

CD0012 — Tanker operation I.question: During the laden voyage it may be necessary to adjust the cargo tank pressure, either by venting VOC, or topping up the tank pressure by inert gas. There are procedures for carrying out and recording these actions. Where would details of the procedures be found?
options: In the vessel’s VOC Management Plan.
In the vessel’s SOPEP.
In the chief engineer’s standing orders.
In the vessel’s inert gas manual.
CD0012 — Tanker operation I.answer: In the vessel’s VOC Management Plan.

CD0012 — Tanker operation I.question: Some busy crude oil loading ports operate an early departure procedure. What is the main feature of the early departure procedure?
options: The vessel is permitted to sail without fully completed official cargo documents in order to speed up port turnaround.
The vessel is permitted to sail as soon as the agent has received the ship’s cargo figures.
The vessel can sail as soon as the cargo surveyors have completed the cargo calculations.
The vessel is permitted to sail without Port Clearance.
CD0012 — Tanker operation I.answer: The vessel is permitted to sail without fully completed official cargo documents in order to speed up port turnaround.

CD0012 — Tanker operation I.question: There are various checklists currently used onboard oil tankers one of which is the pre-departure checklist. What is the main purpose of the pre-departure check list?
options: To verify and document that the vessel is prepared and seaworthy for the next sea passage.
To provide the information required by the agent prior departure.
To ensure that all crew are on board and well rested.
To verify that the loading is completed and all ballast tanks are empty.
CD0012 — Tanker operation I.answer: To verify and document that the vessel is prepared and seaworthy for the next sea passage.

CD0012 — Tanker operation I.question: When early departure procedure is accepted, who signs the official documents?
options: The Master.
The port State control authorities.
The Loading Master.
The agent.
CD0012 — Tanker operation I.answer: The Master.

CD0012 — Tanker operation I.question: All ships, including tankers are issued with orders including voyage orders. Who would normally issue a voyage order?
options: Either the ship owners or ship operators or the charterers.
The cargo owners.
The agent at the discharge, or loading port.
The port authorities.
CD0012 — Tanker operation I.answer: Either the ship owners or ship operators or the charterers.

CD0012 — Tanker operation I.question: What does the three word acronym LOT stand for in relation to the cargo operations of crude oil tankers?
options: Load on Top.
Loaded oil tanker.
Level oil tanks.
Liquid oil tanks.
CD0012 — Tanker operation I.answer: Load on Top.

CD0012 — Tanker operation I.question: Who is normally first to board the vessel after it is securely moored alongside the berth?
options: The quarantine and customs officers.
The port facility security officer.
The loading master
The charterer’s agent.
CD0012 — Tanker operation I.answer: The quarantine and customs officers.

CD0012 — Tanker operation I.question: Which two persons would normally be responsible for agreeing the loading plan for an oil tanker prior to the vessel loading cargo?
options: The chief officer and the loading master.
The ship’s master and the agent.
The loading master and the cargo surveyors.
The ship’s master and the chief officer.
CD0012 — Tanker operation I.answer: The chief officer and the loading master.

CD0012 — Tanker operation I.question: Who is normally in charge on deck during cargo hose connection operations on an oil tanker?
options: The duty deck officer under the supervision of the chief officer.
The loading master.
The bosun under the supervision of the duty deck officer.
The ship’s master.
CD0012 — Tanker operation I.answer: The duty deck officer under the supervision of the chief officer.

CD0012 — Tanker operation I.question: Where oil loading ports operate an early departure procedure, EDP, Who must agree to accept to operate with procedure prior to arrival at the load port?
options: The ship owner or operator and the charterers.
The shippers.
The Protection & Indemnity (P&I) Club.
The Master.
CD0012 — Tanker operation I.answer: The ship owner or operator and the charterers.

CD0012 — Tanker operation I.question: All tankers have an approved Loading Manual on board. Which body approves the Loading Manual?
options: The classification Society to which the ship is classed.
The ship’s building yard.
The National Maritime Authority.
The ship owner’s/Operator’s Technical Department.
CD0012 — Tanker operation I.answer: The classification Society to which the ship is classed.

CD0012 — Tanker operation I.question: What is the basis for making a loading plan on an oil tanker?
options: The loading order.
The reception facilities in the discharge port.
The loading rate.
The vessel’s total loading capacity.
CD0012 — Tanker operation I.answer: The loading order.

CD0012 — Tanker operation I.question: Crude oil tankers often load the next cargo on top of the residue or slops from the previous cargo Who decides if the vessel is to Load on Top of the slops?
options: The charterers.
The ship owner or operator.
The cargo owner.
The cargo receiver.
CD0012 — Tanker operation I.answer: The charterers.

CD0012 — Tanker operation I.question: All oil tankers are required to complete a pre-arrival check list. How are negative answers in the pre-arrival check list handled?
options: They should be reported to the Ship Owner/Operator.
They should be reported to the owner’s agent at discharge port.
The Master calls the Chief Officer and Chief Eng. for a meeting.
The negative answer doesn’t need to be reported it is just entered in the weekly work program.
CD0012 — Tanker operation I.answer: They should be reported to the Ship Owner/Operator.

CD0012 — Tanker operation I.question: Some crude oil loading ports operate an early departure procedure, EDP. Why is EDP used in some ports?
options: In order to make a quick turn-around and not cause delay at the terminal.
Because of a comprehensive and time-consuming handling of cargo documents.
The charterers want to check the figures before the Bills of Lading are issued.
Too expensive to have the vessel waiting for the cargo documents.
CD0012 — Tanker operation I.answer: In order to make a quick turn-around and not cause delay at the terminal.

CD0012 — Tanker operation I.question: Ballast water carried on board oil tankers is governed by stringent regulations. Which one of the given options includes the regulations covering ballast water for crude oil tankers?
options: Ballast Water Management Convention.
International Convention on Load Lines for Ships.
Oil Companies International Marine Forum (OCIMF) guidelines.
The International Convention for the Safety of Life at Sea.
CD0012 — Tanker operation I.answer: Ballast Water Management Convention.

CD0012 — Tanker operation I.question: The cargo figures for the official Bill of Lading are determined following completion of loading operations for a crude oil tanker. Which figures are the figures for the Bill of Lading initially based on?
options: The terminal (shore) figures.
The ship’s figures calculated by the Chief Officer.
The ship’s figures calculated by the cargo surveyors.
The figures given by the cargo owners.
CD0012 — Tanker operation I.answer: The terminal (shore) figures.

CD0012 — Tanker operation I.question: On large crude oil tankers, why is it good practice to have the vessel as close to even keel as possible and with zero list when topping off the tanks?
options: In order to reach the correct quantity in the tanks.
The SOLAS regulations require no list when a vessel leaves port.
In order to read the draught marks correct.
In order to assist the port authorities to check the mid ship loading marks.
CD0012 — Tanker operation I.answer: In order to reach the correct quantity in the tanks.

CD0012 — Tanker operation I.question: All ballast handling must be recorded in dedicated forms. Where are these forms usually found onboard a crude oil tanker?
options: In the Water Ballast Management Plan.
In the SOPEP.
In the OPA 90 VRP.
In the company’s TQM system.
CD0012 — Tanker operation I.answer: In the Water Ballast Management Plan.

CD0012 — Tanker operation I.question: When the Master on a VLCC receives following instruction: “After completion discharge at Rotterdam, proceed to AG via Suez, intention full cargo Ras Tanura/Ju’aymah for NW Europe incl. Med.Sea. Pls. advise bunker requirements ex. barge Fujairah”. What kind of order is this?
options: Voyage order.
Loading order.
Basis for a complete voyage passage plan.
Preliminary loading order.
CD0012 — Tanker operation I.answer: Voyage order.

CD0012 — Tanker operation I.question: It is required that the condition of the ballast tanks on a crude oil tanker are recorded following inspection. Where are the results of these inspections normally recorded?
options: In the vessel’s Planned Maintenance System (PMS).
In the Chief Engineer’s files.
In the Chief Officer’s files.
In the owner’s or operator’s Vetting department.
CD0012 — Tanker operation I.answer: In the vessel’s Planned Maintenance System (PMS).

CD0012 — Tanker operation I.question: Why is it less important if crude oil tankers receive a late loading order compared to chemical, gas and product tankers?
options: Crude oil tankers have less tank preparations prior to loading.
Crude oil tankers have less ROB.
Crude oil tankers always carry the same cargo grade.
Crude oil tankers always Load on Top
CD0012 — Tanker operation I.answer: Crude oil tankers have less tank preparations prior to loading.

CD0012 — Tanker operation I.question: When the vessel is securely moored alongside the discharge terminal, who should be the first to board the vessel?
options: The quarantine and customs officers.
The local agent.
The loading master and terminal representatives.
The terminal’s security officer.
CD0012 — Tanker operation I.answer: The quarantine and customs officers.

CD0012 — Tanker operation I.question: When the Master of a VLCC receives the following instruction: “After completion discharge at US Gulf, proceed to Fujairah for order”. What kind of order is this?
options: Voyage order.
Loading order.
Preliminary loading order.
Basis for a complete passage plan.
CD0012 — Tanker operation I.answer: Voyage order.

CD0012 — Tanker operation I.question: Who is responsible for developing and implementing an International Safety Management System on board?
options: The ship owner or operator.
The Master.
The National Maritime Authority.
The classification society to which the ship is classed.
CD0012 — Tanker operation I.answer: The ship owner or operator.

CD0012 — Tanker operation I.question: After an oil tanker has completed loading operations and the cargo documents have been cleared, the ship’s Master will be given permission to leave the port. What is the term normally used for this permission?
options: Port clearance.
Port dues paid, vessel free to depart.
Customs clearance.
Vessel’s departure permission.
CD0012 — Tanker operation I.answer: Port clearance.

CD0012 — Tanker operation I.question: Once the vessel has been cleared by the quarantine and customs authorities, the independent cargo surveyors may board the vessel. Who are the cargo surveyors representing?
options: The surveyors are representing the shippers and cargo owners or charterers.
The cargo surveyors are representing the ship owner and the cargo owner.
The cargo surveyors are representing the vessel’s P & I Club.
The cargo surveyors are representing the National Customs Office.
CD0012 — Tanker operation I.answer: The surveyors are representing the shippers and cargo owners or charterers.

CD0012 — Tanker operation I.question: The duty deck officer is required to complete all details of cargo operations in the ‘time sheet’. Is the ‘time sheet’ normally considered to be part of the official cargo documentation?
options: Yes, the time sheet is considered to be part of the official documentation.
No, it is only used for calculating crew overtime.
No, it is only for the ship owner’s or operator’s internal use.
No, it is only required by the agent.
CD0012 — Tanker operation I.answer: Yes, the time sheet is considered to be part of the official documentation.

CD0012 — Tanker operation I.question: Who would normally sign all of the cargo documentation prior to departure once a crude oil tanker is finished loading?
options: The ship’s Master and the shippers.
The ship’s Master and the agent.
The chief officer and the loading master.
The ship's Master and the cargo surveyors.
CD0012 — Tanker operation I.answer: The ship’s Master and the shippers.

CD0012 — Tanker operation I.question: The laden voyage is often used as an opportunity to carry out internal inspection of ballast tanks of a crude oil tanker. What is the normal frequency for inspection of ballast tanks on a crude oil tanker?
options: Annually.
Every 6 months.
24 months.
36 months.
CD0012 — Tanker operation I.answer: Annually.

CD0012 — Tanker operation I.question: During cargo loading and discharge of an oil tanker the cargo hoses or loading arms must be connected. Is connection of cargo hoses (arms) part of the vessel’s risk assessment?
options: Yes, it is always part of the vessel’s risk assessment.
Yes, but only when the ship’s own hoses are being used.
Yes, but only when visiting a new port.
No, it is covered by the terminal risk assessment.
CD0012 — Tanker operation I.answer: Yes, it is always part of the vessel’s risk assessment.

CD0012 — Tanker operation I.question: The requirements for reporting of oil spills, and situations that may lead to an oil spill are strictly regulated. Where, onboard ship, are the details of these reporting procedures normally found?
options: In the Shipboard Oil Pollution Emergency Plan (SOPEP).
In the Oil Companies International Marine Forum (OCIMF) Guidelines.
In the vessel’s Damage Stability Manual.
In the MARPOL Annex IV regulations.
CD0012 — Tanker operation I.answer: In the Shipboard Oil Pollution Emergency Plan (SOPEP).

CD0012 — Tanker operation I.question: When the Master on a VLCC receives following instruction: “On completion bunkering at Fujairah, proceed to Kharg Island and load full cargo Iranian Light crude. Disport Antifer, France. Pls. advise cargo intake”. What kind of order is this?
options: Loading order.
Voyage order.
Loading - and discharge order.
Preliminary loading order.
CD0012 — Tanker operation I.answer: Loading order.

CD0012 — Tanker operation I.question: Prior to commencement of loading an oil tanker the independent cargo surveyors carry out a tank survey. What do they survey and calculate?
options: The on board quantity, OBQ.
The total slop and bunker on board.
The total oil and water remaining on board.
The vessel’s experience factor.
CD0012 — Tanker operation I.answer: The on board quantity, OBQ.

CD0013 — Tanker operation II.question: It is a requirement that a record of maintenance and tests of the vessel’s fire fighting equipment is kept on board an oil tanker. Which regulations require this?
options: The International Convention on Safety of Life at Sea (SOLAS).
The ISM Code.
The IMO MARPOL Annex I regulations.
The International Labour Convention (ILO).
CD0013 — Tanker operation II.answer: The International Convention on Safety of Life at Sea (SOLAS).

CD0013 — Tanker operation II.question: Where would the information relating to a crude oil’s flammable and health hazard characteristics normally be found onboard an oil tanker?
options: In the Material Safety Data Sheet.
In the loading instruction.
In the Bulk Chemical (BC) Code.
In the cargo’s Quality certificate.
CD0013 — Tanker operation II.answer: In the Material Safety Data Sheet.

CD0013 — Tanker operation II.question: In a discharge port an independent cargo surveyor will often board an oil tanker. Who does the surveyor normally represent while onboard?
options: The cargo receivers and charterers.
The ship owner.
The P & I Club.
The terminal.

CD0013 — Tanker operation II.question: Who is in normally in charge of connecting the cargo hoses prior to discharge of an oil tanker?
options: The duty deck officer under the supervision of chief officer.
The loading master.
The pumpman
The bosun and deckhands.
CD0013 — Tanker operation II.answer: The duty deck officer under the supervision of chief officer.

CD0013 — Tanker operation II.question: The main purpose of purging cargo tanks with Inert Gas (IG) is to prevent explosive atmosphere in the tanks. What are the standard requirements for oxygen content in the IG supply line and in the cargo tanks?
options: Maximum 5% and 8% respectively
Maximum 6% and 11% respectively
Maximum 0% and 5% respectively
Maximum 2% and 5% respectively

CD0013 — Tanker operation II.question: What is normally calculated by the cargo surveyors following completion of cargo discharge of an oil tanker?
options: Total quantity of cargo remaining on board (R.O.B).
Liquid cargo remaining in the pipelines.
Total quantity of oil and water remaining on the vessel.
The experience factor.
CD0013 — Tanker operation II.answer: Total quantity of cargo remaining on board (R.O.B).

CD0013 — Tanker operation II.question: Which of the given options would normally be done to help avoid any under- pressure in the cargo tanks of a crude oil tanker when starting the discharge?
options: Start the IG plant.
Open the mast riser.
Increase the cargo pumps speed.
Continue pumping until the P/V valves open.

CD0013 — Tanker operation II.question: Who would normally issue the orders for the manifold valves to be opened and the discharge of an oil tanker to be started?
options: The loading master.
The chief officer.
The ship’s Master.
The chief officer and the duty deck officer in co-operation.

CD0013 — Tanker operation II.question: Who would normally issue the discharge order to the ship’s Master of an oil tanker?
options: Owner/Operator or Charterer.
The cargo receiver.
The agent in discharge port.
The cargo owner.

CD0013 — Tanker operation II.question: Crude oil washing (COW) is strictly regulated under MARPOL. Who would normally decide that the vessel should carry out COW operations during discharge?
options: The charterers.
The Master.
The cargo receiver.
The port Authority.

CD0013 — Tanker operation II.question: When the chief officer is working out the discharge plan for an oil tanker what information does he base the plan on?
options: The discharge instruction.
The voyage order.
The cargo distribution.
The terminal’s reception capacity.

CD0013 — Tanker operation II.question: When the discharge of an oil tanker is completed, who signs the chief officer’s reception documents for cargo discharged?
options: The loading master.
The independent cargo surveyor.
The agent.
The port authority.

CD0013 — Tanker operation II.question: Following completion of cargo discharge an oil tanker requires certain documentation before being allowed to sail. Which of the documents given in the options allows the vessel to leave the port?
options: Port clearance.
Receipt for cargo discharged.
Receipt for paid port fee.
Receipt for paid light dues.

CD0013 — Tanker operation II.question: Which of the given options may be considered as the most critical operation onboard an oil tanker?
options: Gas freeing and entering cargo tanks.
Hot work outside the engine room.
Tank washing.
Crude Oil Washing.
CD0013 — Tanker operation II.answer: Gas freeing and entering cargo tanks.

CD0013 — Tanker operation II.question: For what period of time must the print rolls of the ODME as fitted on an oil tanker be retained for inspection?
options: 3 years
6 months
12 months
5 years

CD0013 — Tanker operation II.question: Under which regulations are COW regulated?
options: MARPOL Annex I.
Intern. Convention on Safety of Life at Sea (SOLAS).
Convention on Intern. Regulations for Preventing Collisions at Sea (COLREG).
International Convention on Load Lines (Int. LL Conv.)

CD0013 — Tanker operation II.question: Crude oil tankers are fitted with an ODME. What is the main purpose of the ODME?
options: To prevent oil pollution.
To document how much oil is discharged over board.
To reduce the amount of oil in the slop tanks.
To ensure that the secondary slop tank is kept free of oil.

CD0013 — Tanker operation II.question: What are the requirements for the oxygen and hydrocarbon gas concentration for safe entry into a cargo tank?
options: Oxygen 21% and HC gas less than 1 % LEL
Oxygen 18.5 % and HC 2 %
Oxygen 19.5 % and HC 9 % UEL
Oxygen 20.8 % and HC 1.5 % LEL
CD0013 — Tanker operation II.answer: Oxygen 21% and HC gas less than 1 % LEL

CD0013 — Tanker operation II.question: During discharge and COW operations of a crude oil tanker it is important to monitor the Inert Gas (IG) quality and pressure. What is the procedure if the IG system fails during such operation?
options: Stop the discharge and COW.
Stop the COW operation and reduce the discharge rate.
Continue the operation and rectify the IG failure.
Continue the operation as the P/V valves will open if the tanks go into an under-pressure condition.

CD0013 — Tanker operation II.question: When the Loading Master orders the discharge to start at slow rate, a certain amount of cargo has to be discharged before full rate is ordered. What is this discharge sequence called?
options: Line displacement.
Line test.
Flow control.
Shore clearing.

CD0013 — Tanker operation II.question: When carrying out COW operations onboard a crude oil tanker the regulations require that certain check lists are used. Where onboard are these check lists available and how many of them are required?
options: In the COW Manual and 3 different check lists are required.
In the SOPEP Manual and 2 check lists are required.
In the company’s ISM/TQM system and 3 different check lists are required.
In the International Safety Guide for Oil Tankers and Terminals (ISGOTT) and 3 check lists are required.
CD0013 — Tanker operation II.answer: In the COW Manual and 3 different check lists are required.

CD0013 — Tanker operation II.question: When the Master of a VLCC receives following instruction: “After completion loading at Ras Tanura, proceed to dis.port NW Europe incl. Med.Sea and Scandinavia, via Cape”. What kind of order is this?
options: Voyage order.
Discharge order.
Preliminary discharge order.
Basis for a complete voyage plan.

CD0013 — Tanker operation II.question: Which activity is considered to be the most critical on an oil tanker?
options: Gas freeing and entering a cargo tank.
Crude oil washing (COW).
Hot work in the engine room.
Tank cleaning.
CD0013 — Tanker operation II.answer: Gas freeing and entering a cargo tank.

CD0013 — Tanker operation II.question: The cargo tanks on a crude oil tanker are required to be inspected internally. How often must internal inspection of the cargo tanks normally be carried out?
options: At intervals not exceeding 30 months.
At intervals not exceeding 12 months.
Prior to each dry docking.
During the annual survey by Class.

CD0013 — Tanker operation II.question: According to the MARPOL Annex I regulations, the cargo tanks of a crude oil tanker need to be crude oil washed for sludge control. What are the requirements in relation to crude oil washing of cargo tanks?
options: No tank need to be crude oil washed more than once in every four months.
All tanks to be crude oil washed annually.
One quarter of the total number of tanks to be crude oil washed every discharge.
The slop tanks and 4 other tanks to be crude oil washed every discharge.
CD0013 — Tanker operation II.answer: No tank need to be crude oil washed more than once in every four months.

CD0013 — Tanker operation II.question: Operating oil tankers poses a risk to personnel and the environment. Which of the given options is considered as the main source of information on guidelines and recommendations for safe operation of oil tankers?
options: International Safety Guide for Oil Tankers and Terminals (ISGOTT)
The Oil Companies International Marine Forum (OCIMF)
The International Convention on Safety of Life at Sea (SOLAS)
IMO MARPOL Annex I
CD0013 — Tanker operation II.answer: International Safety Guide for Oil Tankers and Terminals (ISGOTT)

CD0013 — Tanker operation II.question: Oil tankers are required to complete pre-arrival check list before entering port. How are negative answers in the pre-arrival check list handled?
options: Reported to the Ship Owner/Operator.
Reported to the owner’s agent at discharge port.
The Master calls the Chief Officer and Chief Eng. for a meeting.
The negative answer is entered in the weekly work program.

CD0013 — Tanker operation II.question: The IG produced on the crude oil tankers will normally contain some oxygen. What are the requirements for the Oxygen content in the IG during discharge, cow and tank cleaning?
options: 5% in the IG supply and 8% in the tank atmosphere.
3% in the IG supply and 5% in the tank atmosphere.
5% in the IG supply and 5% in the tank atmosphere.
8% in the IG supply and 15% in the tank atmosphere.
CD0013 — Tanker operation II.answer: 5% in the IG supply and 8% in the tank atmosphere.

CD0013 — Tanker operation II.question: What was the size limitation when the MARPOL Annex I made COW mandatory for new crude oil tankers?
options: Tankers of 20.000 tons deadweight and above.
Tankers of 10.000 tons deadweight and above.
Tankers of 50.000 tons deadweight and above.
Tankers of 70.000 tons deadweight and above.
CD0013 — Tanker operation II.answer: Tankers of 20.000 tons deadweight and above.

CD0013 — Tanker operation II.question: Crude oil washing was made mandatory for new tankers by the 1978 Protocol to the MARPOL Convention. What was the main reason for this requirement?
options: To prevent oil pollution.
To increase the amount of cargo discharged.
To avoid the need for sludge removal by hand.
To reduce the need for water washing.

CD0013 — Tanker operation II.question: What is it that independent cargo surveyors normally measure and calculate prior to commencement of discharge operations by an oil tanker?
options: The cargo figures on arrival.
The remaining onboard quantity (R.O.B.).
The total ship figures on arrival.
The Onboard quantity (O.B.Q.).

CD0013 — Tanker operation II.question: When entering a cargo tank, or enclosed space, it is by regulations required to record such entry. Where should the entry into the tank be recorded?
options: The Deck Log Book.
The Oil Record Book Part II.
The Oil Record Book Part I.
In the PMS tank inspection records.
