CD0013 — Tanker operation II.question: When the Master receives instruction to proceed to Rotterdam and discharge all cargo at a port such as Europoort Maatschap Tankfarm, who would normally issue this instruction?
options: The ship owner/operator or charterers.
The cargo owner.
The charterer’s agent in Rotterdam.
The owner’s agent in Rotterdam.
The cargo receiver at Europoort.

CD0013 — Tanker operation II.question: The discharge plan of an oil tanker will normally include ballast operations. According to IMO regulations all ballast handling is required to be recorded. Where are ballast handling operations normally recorded onboard an oil tanker?
options: In the Ballast Water Management Plan’s record forms.
In the Deck Log Book.
In the Pump Log.
In the Oil Record Book Part II
CD0013 — Tanker operation II.answer: In the Ballast Water Management Plan’s record forms.

CD0013 — Tanker operation II.question: When the discharge of an oil tanker is completed, the cargo surveyors start surveying the cargo tanks. What action would be expected to be taken if an unacceptable quantity of cargo oil remains on board?
options: The cargo surveyors issue a Letter of Protest on behalf of the cargo receivers and charterers.
The cargo surveyors request stripping of the tanks to be resumed.
The cargo surveyors request the terminal to assist with a new tank survey.
The vessel will be detained until all cargo oil is discharged.
CD0013 — Tanker operation II.answer: The cargo surveyors issue a Letter of Protest on behalf of the cargo receivers and charterers.

CD0013 — Tanker operation II.question: Once an oil tanker is cleared by the quarantine and customs authorities the independent cargo surveyors can normally board the vessel. Who do the cargo surveyors usually represent?
options: The surveyors are representing the cargo receivers and cargo owners or charterers.
The cargo surveyors are representing the ship owner and cargo owner.
The cargo surveyors are representing the vessel’s P & I Club.
The cargo surveyors are representing the National Customs Office.
CD0013 — Tanker operation II.answer: The surveyors are representing the cargo receivers and cargo owners or charterers.

CD0013 — Tanker operation II.question: Once an oil tanker is securely moored alongside the discharge terminal, who is normally the first to board the vessel?
options: Quarantine and customs officers.
The local agent.
The loading Master and terminal representatives.
The terminal’s security officer.

CD0013 — Tanker operation II.question: Prior to arrival at a discharge port, a crude oil tanker will require permission to carry out COW operations during discharge. Who would normally need to give permission to carry out COW during discharge operations?
options: The port authority and terminal prior to arrival.
The charterer.
The Ship Owner/Operator.
The cargo receiver gives permission as he is focusing on the best out-turn of the cargo.
CD0013 — Tanker operation II.answer: The port authority and terminal prior to arrival.

CD0013 — Tanker operation II.question: A discharge order may change during the vessel’s voyage. What is the usual reason for such a change to the discharge orders of an oil tanker?
options: The cargo is sold during the voyage.
The cargo receivers are not able to pay for the cargo.
The cargo receivers do not accept the cargo quality specifications.
Congestion at discharge port.
CD0013 — Tanker operation II.answer: The cargo is sold during the voyage.

CD0014 — Vessel Struct. Cond..question: Which one of the following statements about the strength of the hull is most accurate?
options: Factors such as operation in rough weather and damage from cargo work can greatly reduce the strength of the hull
The strength of the ship never changes much after the building stage
The strength of the ship always decreases rapidly in service
Incidental damage from cargo work has no effect on the strength of the hull
CD0014 — Vessel Struct. Cond..answer: Factors such as operation in rough weather and damage from cargo work can greatly reduce the strength of the hull

CD0014 — Vessel Struct. Cond..question: With respect to flat bar cross sections of stiffeners used for the ship’s hull, which one of the following statements is most accurate?
options: Flat bar is relatively poor at resisting buckling
Flat bar is relatively good at resisting buckling
Flat bar is relatively expensive to make
Flat bar is difficult to apply a protective coating to
CD0014 — Vessel Struct. Cond..answer: Flat bar is relatively poor at resisting buckling

CD0014 — Vessel Struct. Cond..question: With respect to framing types for the ship’s hull, which one of the following statements is most accurate?
options: Combination framing uses both transverse and longitudinal framing
Combination framing uses transverse frames and box girders
Combination framing uses longitudinal frames and box girders
Combination framing is required on all new oil tankers
CD0014 — Vessel Struct. Cond..answer: Combination framing uses both transverse and longitudinal framing

CD0014 — Vessel Struct. Cond..question: Which one of the following statements about corrosion is most accurate?
options: Corrosion can greatly reduce the strength of the ship
Corrosion of the hull is relatively unimportant, as there is an allowance for this at the design stage
The strength of the hull always decreases rapidly in service
No permanent loss of hull strength occurs because of operation in heavy weather
CD0014 — Vessel Struct. Cond..answer: Corrosion can greatly reduce the strength of the ship

CD0014 — Vessel Struct. Cond..question: Which one of the following statements about bending of the hull is most accurate?
options: When the hull is hogging, the deck will be in tension whilst the keel will be in compression
When the hull is hogging, the deck will be in compression whilst the keel will be in tension
When the hull is sagging, the deck will be under tension whilst the keel will be in compression
When the hull is sagging, the deck and keel will be under tension
CD0014 — Vessel Struct. Cond..answer: When the hull is hogging, the deck will be in tension whilst the keel will be in compression

CD0014 — Vessel Struct. Cond..question: When the distance between wave crests is equal to the length of the ship’s hull, which one of the following statements is most accurate?
options: When the wave crests are fore and aft, they will make the ship tend to sag
The smallest bending moment caused by the wave motion will be when either the peak or the trough of the wave is at mid-ships
When the wave crests are fore and aft, they will make the ship tend to hog
There will be no overall effect on the hull
CD0014 — Vessel Struct. Cond..answer: When the wave crests are fore and aft, they will make the ship tend to sag

CD0014 — Vessel Struct. Cond..question: With respect to the ship’s hull, which one of the following statements is most accurate?
options: Longitudinal framing tends to be used for longer vessels
Transverse framing tends to be used for longer vessels
Longitudinal and transverse framing should never be used on the same ship
Longitudinal framing cannot resist bending stresses
CD0014 — Vessel Struct. Cond..answer: Longitudinal framing tends to be used for longer vessels

CD0014 — Vessel Struct. Cond..question: With respect to the cross sections of stiffeners used for the ship’s hull, which one of the following statements is most accurate?
options: T-profile performs better in most situations
Angle bar performs better in most situations
Flat bar performs better in most situations
It is difficult to apply protective coatings to Bulb profiles
CD0014 — Vessel Struct. Cond..answer: T-profile performs better in most situations

CD0014 — Vessel Struct. Cond..question: With reference to shear forces on a ship’s hull, which one of the following statements is most accurate?
options: Shear forces cause further stress on the hull in addition to that caused by bending
Shear forces are not significant compared to the stress on the hull caused by bending
Shear forces cancel out some of the stress on the hull caused by bending
Shear stress always opposes the stress on the hull caused by bending
CD0014 — Vessel Struct. Cond..answer: Shear forces cause further stress on the hull in addition to that caused by bending

CD0014 — Vessel Struct. Cond..question: With reference to the stress distribution of a ship’s hull subjected to bending, which one of the following statements is most accurate?
options: The bending stresses will be maximum at the deck and bottom plating and reduce towards the neutral axis at approximately the mid-point of the side plating
The bending stresses will be zero at the deck and bottom plating and increase towards the neutral axis at approximately the mid-point of the side plating
The bending stresses will be equal at the deck, bottom plating and the neutral axis at approximately the mid-point of the side plating
The bending stresses will be maximum at the deck plating and reduce to zero at the bottom plating
CD0014 — Vessel Struct. Cond..answer: The bending stresses will be maximum at the deck and bottom plating and reduce towards the neutral axis at approximately the mid-point of the side plating

CD0014 — Vessel Struct. Cond..question: Which one of the following statements about hull strength is most accurate?
options: A ship regularly operating in heavy weather is subject to many stress reversals which lower the strength of the hull
A ship regularly operating in heavy weather will remain as strong as when new if properly maintained
Fatigue cracking is never related to corrosion
Small Fatigue cracks will normally be okay until the next dry-dock or survey
CD0014 — Vessel Struct. Cond..answer: A ship regularly operating in heavy weather is subject to many stress reversals which lower the strength of the hull

CD0014 — Vessel Struct. Cond..question: With reference to the hull structure, which one of the following statements is most accurate?
options: Fatigue is the reduction in strength of a material due to repeated cycles of stress
Fatigue cracking is most likely when the ship is new
Fatigue is the reduction in strength of a material due to constant high load
If protective coatings are maintained, fatigue will never affect a ship
CD0014 — Vessel Struct. Cond..answer: Fatigue is the reduction in strength of a material due to repeated cycles of stress

CD0014 — Vessel Struct. Cond..question: With reference to the stress distribution along the length of a ship’s hull subjected to bending, which one of the following statements is most accurate?
options: If the ship is evenly loaded, the bending stresses are at a maximum at mid-length
If the ship is evenly loaded, the bending stresses are at a maximum fore and aft
If the ship is evenly loaded, the bending stresses are equal along the length of the ship
If the ship is evenly loaded, the bending stresses are at a minimum at mid-length
CD0014 — Vessel Struct. Cond..answer: If the ship is evenly loaded, the bending stresses are at a maximum at mid-length

CD0014 — Vessel Struct. Cond..question: With reference to water on the deck of a ship, which one of the following statements is most accurate?
options: Sea water coming over the deck will cause downward forces on the ship’s structure and is most likely to affect the fore end of the vessel
Sea water coming over the deck will cause downward forces on the ship’s structure and is most likely to affect the aft end of the vessel
Sea water coming over the deck causes additional buoyancy forces on the ship’s structure
Sea water coming over the deck has little overall effect on large vessels
CD0014 — Vessel Struct. Cond..answer: Sea water coming over the deck will cause downward forces on the ship’s structure and is most likely to affect the fore end of the vessel

CD0014 — Vessel Struct. Cond..question: With regard to looking for defects in the hull structure, which one of the following statements is most accurate?
options: Connections between parts of the structure, or changes of section, are common areas to find defects
Connections between parts of the structure are so strong that they rarely fail
Small cracks in shell plating above the waterline are of no concern
Loss of protective coating above welds is fairly common and of no immediate concern
CD0014 — Vessel Struct. Cond..answer: Connections between parts of the structure, or changes of section, are common areas to find defects

CD0014 — Vessel Struct. Cond..question: With reference to cracking of the hull structure, which one of the following statements is most accurate?
options: Cracks occur when the material can no longer withstand tensile forces
Cracks occur when the material can no longer withstand compressive forces
Corrosion does not affect whether or not cracks occur
Fatigue does not affect whether or not cracks occur
CD0014 — Vessel Struct. Cond..answer: Cracks occur when the material can no longer withstand tensile forces

CD0014 — Vessel Struct. Cond..question: With respect to the ship’s hull, which one of the following statements is most accurate?
options: The main purpose of the longitudinal stiffeners is to resist bending
Longitudinal stiffeners are only used in shorter vessels
Longitudinal stiffeners are only used in longer vessels
The main purpose of the transverse frames is to support the deck structure
CD0014 — Vessel Struct. Cond..answer: The main purpose of the longitudinal stiffeners is to resist bending

CD0014 — Vessel Struct. Cond..question: With regard to shear forces acting on the hull, which one of the following statements is most accurate?
options: Shear force is created when there are two parallel, opposite forces, like gravity and buoyancy
Shear force is created when there are two parallel forces in the same direction, like gravity and buoyancy
Shear force refers to the horizontal force at the forward part of the vessel
Shear force refers to the horizontal force at the aft part of the vessel
CD0014 — Vessel Struct. Cond..answer: Shear force is created when there are two parallel, opposite forces, like gravity and buoyancy

CD0014 — Vessel Struct. Cond..question: With reference to crack formation in the hull structure, which one of the following statements is most accurate?
options: Cracks can occur due to fatigue, corrosion, or sharp changes of section
Cracks occur when the material can no longer withstand compressive forces
Small cracks often occur and are not a significant problem
Cracks in hatch coamings are not a significant problem
CD0014 — Vessel Struct. Cond..answer: Cracks can occur due to fatigue, corrosion, or sharp changes of section

CD0014 — Vessel Struct. Cond..question: With reference to looking for defects in the hull structure, which one of the following statements is most accurate?
options: Indentations in the side and floor plating of Bulk carriers from cargo work can lead to corrosion and cracking
Indentations in the side and floor plating of Bulk carriers from cargo work are usually of no great importance
Large hatch openings on container and bulk vessels do not form part of the structure and therefore do not need close inspection
Double bottom tanks are not usually subject to corrosion
CD0014 — Vessel Struct. Cond..answer: Indentations in the side and floor plating of Bulk carriers from cargo work can lead to corrosion and cracking

CD0014 — Vessel Struct. Cond..question: Which one of the following statements about forces on the ship’s hull is most accurate?
options: Panting is the in and out movement of the shell plating due to the variation in water pressure on the shell plating.
Pounding is most likely to occur when the ship is fully loaded
Panting occurs when the vessel is lifted by the sea and then slams back down on the water
Pounding damage is most likely at mid-ships
CD0014 — Vessel Struct. Cond..answer: Panting is the in and out movement of the shell plating due to the variation in water pressure on the shell plating.

CD0014 — Vessel Struct. Cond..question: With respect to rolling causing stress on the ship’s hull, which one of the following statements is most accurate?
options: Rolling mostly causes stresses in the transverse bulkheads
Rolling mostly causes stresses at the forward part of the ship
Rolling mostly causes stresses at the aft part of the ship
Rolling mostly causes stresses in the longitudinal stiffeners
CD0014 — Vessel Struct. Cond..answer: Rolling mostly causes stresses in the transverse bulkheads

CD0014 — Vessel Struct. Cond..question: With regard to the hulls of Ro-Ro’s and car ferries, which one of the following statements is most accurate?
options: The bow visor and inner door are considered the most vital areas of the hull for inspection on car ferries and Ro-Ro vessels
The bow visor and inner door are above the waterline and therefore less vital than other areas of the hull for inspection on car ferries and Ro-Ro vessels
The deck plating is considered the most vital areas of the hull for inspection on car ferries and Ro-Ro vessels
The bottom plating is considered the most vital areas of the hull for inspection on car ferries and Ro-Ro vessels
CD0014 — Vessel Struct. Cond..answer: The bow visor and inner door are considered the most vital areas of the hull for inspection on car ferries and Ro-Ro vessels

CD0014 — Vessel Struct. Cond..question: For a loaded, simply supported symmetrical beam which one of the following statements about the ^Mresulting bending stresses is most accurate?
options: If the beam is symmetrical, the bending stresses are highest at the outside surfaces and zero along the neutral
If the beam is symmetrical, the bending stresses are zero at the outside surfaces and highest along the neutral
If the beam is symmetrical, the bending stresses are the same throughout any cross-section of the beam
If the beam is symmetrical, the bending stresses are zero throughout any cross-section of the beam
CD0014 — Vessel Struct. Cond..answer: If the beam is symmetrical, the bending stresses are highest at the outside surfaces and zero along the neutral

CD0014 — Vessel Struct. Cond..question: Which one of the following statements about forces on the hull is most accurate?
options: Shear forces on the hull will tend to be high if one hold is fully loaded and the next is empty
Shear forces on the hull will be tend to be high if all holds are evenly loaded
Shear forces on the hull will tend to be high if all holds are empty
Shear forces on the hull will tend to be low if one hold is fully loaded and the next is empty
CD0014 — Vessel Struct. Cond..answer: Shear forces on the hull will tend to be high if one hold is fully loaded and the next is empty

CD0014 — Vessel Struct. Cond..question: With reference to looking for defects in the hull structure around hatch openings, which one of the following statements is most accurate?
options: The hatch corners and hatch coaming brackets need close attention as they are prone to cracking
The deck plating mid way along the length of the hatch needs close attention as it is prone to cracking
The deck plating mid way along the breadth of the hatch needs close attention as it is prone to cracking
Hatch openings do not form part of the structure and therefore do not need close inspection
CD0014 — Vessel Struct. Cond..answer: The hatch corners and hatch coaming brackets need close attention as they are prone to cracking

CD0014 — Vessel Struct. Cond..question: With reference to the hull structure, which one of the following statements is most accurate?
options: Resistance to buckling depends on the length and cross section of the stiffener or girder
Resistance to buckling depends only on the length of the stiffener or girder
Resistance to buckling depends only on the cross section of the stiffener or girder
Buckling can occur in tension or compression
CD0014 — Vessel Struct. Cond..answer: Resistance to buckling depends on the length and cross section of the stiffener or girder

CD0014 — Vessel Struct. Cond..question: With reference to static and dynamic forces acting on the hull, which one of the following statements is most accurate?
options: High static forces, for instance due to poor cargo loading, mean that the vessel is less safe when operating in heavy weather
Provided the maximum static loading for the hull has not been exceeded, the vessel should be safe in any weather conditions
Dynamic loads on the vessel are insignificant compared to the weight of cargo and ballast
Static forces on the vessel are insignificant compared to sea forces
CD0014 — Vessel Struct. Cond..answer: High static forces, for instance due to poor cargo loading, mean that the vessel is less safe when operating in heavy weather

CD0014 — Vessel Struct. Cond..question: Which one of the following statements about hull inspections is most accurate?
options: Ship’s crew should regularly inspect the cargo holds, hatch covers and ballast tanks with a view to detecting damage and defects
Ship’s crew are not allowed to inspect the cargo holds, hatch covers and ballast tanks
There is no need to detect damage and defects between surveys
Ship’s crew have insufficient training to inspect the cargo holds, hatch covers and ballast tanks with a view to detecting damage and defects.
CD0014 — Vessel Struct. Cond..answer: Ship’s crew should regularly inspect the cargo holds, hatch covers and ballast tanks with a view to detecting damage and defects

CD0014 — Vessel Struct. Cond..question: For a loaded, simply supported beam which one of the following statements about compressive and tensile forces is most accurate?
options: The load side is under compression and the opposite side is under tension
The load side is under tension and the opposite side is under compression
Both the load side and the opposite side are under tension
Both the load side and the opposite side are under compression
CD0014 — Vessel Struct. Cond..answer: The load side is under compression and the opposite side is under tension

CD0014 — Vessel Struct. Cond..question: With respect to bending stresses on the ship’s hull, which one of the following statements is most accurate?
options: Bending stresses will normally be highest at mid length and at the deck and bottom plating levels
Bending stresses will normally be highest fore and aft and at the deck and bottom plating levels
Bending stresses will normally be highest at mid length and half way between the deck and bottom plating levels
Bending stresses will normally be highest in way of the engine room and half way between the deck and bottom plating levels
CD0014 — Vessel Struct. Cond..answer: Bending stresses will normally be highest at mid length and at the deck and bottom plating levels

CD0014 — Vessel Struct. Cond..question: With reference to stiffening of side shell plating, which one of the following statements is most accurate?
options: The middle and ends of stiffeners and girders will be subject to the highest bending stress
The middle and ends of stiffeners and girders will be subject to zero bending stress
Bending stress is equal along the entire length of stiffeners and girders
The ends of stiffeners and girders will be subject to zero bending stress
CD0014 — Vessel Struct. Cond..answer: The middle and ends of stiffeners and girders will be subject to the highest bending stress

CD0014 — Vessel Struct. Cond..question: Which one of these IMO publications requires that Bulk Carriers have a loading plan?
options: SOLAS
COLREG
Load line
MARPOL
CD0014 — Vessel Struct. Cond..answer: SOLAS

CD0014 — Vessel Struct. Cond..question: With reference to the forces acting on the hull, which one of the following statements is most accurate?
options: Panting, pounding, and sloshing of liquids in tanks are examples of dynamic forces
Static forces tend to cancel out dynamic forces
The weight of fuel, cargo, fresh water and ballast are examples of dynamic forces
Dynamic forces are always small compared to static forces
CD0014 — Vessel Struct. Cond..answer: Panting, pounding, and sloshing of liquids in tanks are examples of dynamic forces

CD0014 — Vessel Struct. Cond..question: For a loaded, simply supported beam with uneven loading, which one of the following statements about the loading of the supports is most accurate?
options: If the loading is uneven, the support nearest to the load has the greatest force
If the loading is uneven, the support furthest from the load has the greatest force
Even if the loading is uneven, each support carries equal force
Even if the loading is uneven, the reactions at each support will be zero.
CD0014 — Vessel Struct. Cond..answer: If the loading is uneven, the support nearest to the load has the greatest force

CD0014 — Vessel Struct. Cond..question: For an evenly loaded, simply supported beam which one of the following statements about the bending stress is most accurate?
options: The bending stress is greatest half way along the length of the beam
The ends of the beam cannot move
The bending stress is greatest at each end
The bending stress is zero half way along the length of the beam
CD0014 — Vessel Struct. Cond..answer: The bending stress is greatest half way along the length of the beam

CD0014 — Vessel Struct. Cond..question: Which one of the following statements about sloshing of fluid in tanks is most accurate?
options: Excessive forces from fluids sloshing in tanks can be prevented by not having them between 20% and 90% full
Excessive forces from fluids sloshing in tanks can be prevented by having them between 20% and 90% full
Excessive forces from fluids sloshing in tanks can only be prevented by  having them completely full
Excessive forces from fluids sloshing in tanks can be prevented by having them only half full
CD0014 — Vessel Struct. Cond..answer: Excessive forces from fluids sloshing in tanks can be prevented by not having them between 20% and 90% full

CD0014 — Vessel Struct. Cond..question: Which one of the following statements about the loads on the hull is most accurate?
options: Reducing the dynamic loads on the hull by slowing down or altering course in heavy weather is effective in both increasing safety and maintaining the strength of the vessel
Little can be done in heavy weather to reduce the dynamic loads on the hull
Static loads on the hull can be reduced by slowing down or altering course
Reducing the dynamic loads on the hull by slowing down or altering course in heavy weather should only be considered in an emergency for safety reasons
CD0014 — Vessel Struct. Cond..answer: Reducing the dynamic loads on the hull by slowing down or altering course in heavy weather is effective in both increasing safety and maintaining the strength of the vessel

CD0014 — Vessel Struct. Cond..question: For an evenly loaded built-in beam, which one of the following statements is most accurate?
options: The bending stress is zero at mid length
The bending stress is zero at the ends
The bending stress is high at mid length and at the ends
Bending stress is zero along the whole length
CD0014 — Vessel Struct. Cond..answer: The bending stress is high at mid length and at the ends

CD0014 — Vessel Struct. Cond..question: Which one of the following statements about forces on beams is most accurate?
options: Vertical forces applied to a beam cause only compression or tension
Vertical forces applied to a beam cause compression, tension, shear and bending
Vertical forces applied to a beam only cause bending
Vertical forces applied to a beam only cause shear forces
CD0014 — Vessel Struct. Cond..answer: Vertical forces applied to a beam cause compression, tension, shear and bending

CD0014 — Vessel Struct. Cond..question: Which one of the following statements about forces on beams is most accurate?
options: If a beam is loaded symmetrically the reactions at each support will be the same
If a beam is loaded symmetrically the reactions at each support will be different.
If a beam is loaded symmetrically the reactions at each support will be equal to the full load.
If a beam is loaded symmetrically the reactions at each support will be zero.
CD0014 — Vessel Struct. Cond..answer: If a beam is loaded symmetrically the reactions at each support will be the same

CD0014 — Vessel Struct. Cond..question: For an evenly loaded, simply supported beam which one of the following statements is most accurate?
options: The ends of the beam are fixed
The bending stress is greatest at mid length
The bending stress is greatest at the ends
The bending stress is zero at mid length
CD0014 — Vessel Struct. Cond..answer: The bending stress is greatest at mid length

CD0014 — Vessel Struct. Cond..question: Which one of the following statements about fatigue is most accurate?
options: Because fatigue requires millions of stress reversals, it is unlikely to affect most ships
Fatigue cracking is made more likely by surface corrosion and sudden changes of section
The strength of the hull is constant throughout its lifetime.
Operation in heavy weather is not related to fatigue.
CD0014 — Vessel Struct. Cond..answer: Fatigue cracking is made more likely by surface corrosion and sudden changes of section

CD0014 — Vessel Struct. Cond..question: With reference to stiffening of side shell plating, which one of the following statements is most accurate?
options: The middle and ends of stiffeners and girders will be subject to the highest bending stress
The middle and ends of stiffeners and girders will be subject to the lowest bending stress.
The middle of stiffeners and girders will be subject to zero bending stress.
The ends of stiffeners and girders will be subject to zero bending stress
CD0014 — Vessel Struct. Cond..answer: The middle and ends of stiffeners and girders will be subject to the highest bending stress

CD0014 — Vessel Struct. Cond..question: With regard to the hull construction of gas carriers, which one of the following statements is most accurate?
options: The cargo tanks make a large contribution to the strength of the hull
The cargo tanks do not contribute to the strength of the hull structure
Only the cargo tanks need to be made of low temperature steel
The cargo tanks account for about 20% of the hull strength
CD0014 — Vessel Struct. Cond..answer: The cargo tanks do not contribute to the strength of the hull structure

CD0014 — Vessel Struct. Cond..question: Which one of the following statements about corrosion is most accurate?
options: Corrosion leads to loss of strength and promotes cracking
Corrosion leads to some loss of strength only
Corrosion of some ballast tank surfaces is to be expected and is not a major problem.
Corrosion of side plating is to be expected and is not a major problem.
CD0014 — Vessel Struct. Cond..answer: Corrosion leads to loss of strength and promotes cracking

CD0014 — Vessel Struct. Cond..question: Which one of the following statements is most accurate?
options: High static forces, for instance due to poor cargo loading, reduce the ability of the hull to resist the dynamic loads experienced in heavy weather
Provided the maximum static loading for the hull has not been exceeded, the vessel should be safe in any weather conditions
Dynamic loads on the vessel are insignificant compared to the cargo load
Static forces on the vessel are insignificant compared to sea forces
CD0014 — Vessel Struct. Cond..answer: High static forces, for instance due to poor cargo loading, reduce the ability of the hull to resist the dynamic loads experienced in heavy weather

CD0014 — Vessel Struct. Cond..question: Which one of the following statements about bending of the hull is most accurate?
options: When the hull is hogging, the deck will be under compression whilst the keel will be in tension.
When the hull is sagging, the deck will be under compression whilst the keel will be in tension.
When the hull is sagging, the deck will be under tension whilst the keel will be in compression.
When the hull is sagging, the deck and keel will be under compression.
CD0014 — Vessel Struct. Cond..answer: When the hull is sagging, the deck will be under compression whilst the keel will be in tension.

CD0014 — Vessel Struct. Cond..question: Which one of the following statements is most accurate?
options: The highest forces due to wave action occur when the distance between wave crests is equal to half the length of the ship
The highest forces due to wave action occur when the distance between wave crests is equal to twice the length of the ship.
The highest forces due to wave action occur when the distance between wave crests is equal to one quarter of the length of the ship.
The highest forces due to wave action occur when the distance between wave crests is equal to the length of the ship.
CD0014 — Vessel Struct. Cond..answer: The highest forces due to wave action occur when the distance between wave crests is equal to the length of the ship.

CD0014 — Vessel Struct. Cond..question: Which one of the following statements is most accurate?
options: Pounding is the in and out movement of the shell plating due to the variation in water pressure on the shell plating.
Pounding is most likely to occur when the ship is fully loaded
Panting occurs when the vessel is lifted by the sea and then slams back down on the water.
Pounding occurs when the vessel is lifted by the sea and then slams back down on the water
CD0014 — Vessel Struct. Cond..answer: Pounding occurs when the vessel is lifted by the sea and then slams back down on the water

CD0014 — Vessel Struct. Cond..question: Which one of the following statements about the strength of the hull is most accurate?
options: The strength of the ship is fixed at the design stage.
The strength of the ship is fixed after the building stage
The strength of the ship always decreases rapidly in service
Factors such as regular operation in heavy weather and damage from cargo work reduce the strength of the ship
CD0014 — Vessel Struct. Cond..answer: Factors such as regular operation in heavy weather and damage from cargo work reduce the strength of the ship

CD0014 — Vessel Struct. Cond..question: For an evenly loaded ship, which one of the following statements is most accurate?
options: The bending stresses acting on the hull will normally be maximum half way along its length
The bending stresses acting on the hull will normally be maximum at the accommodation
The bending stresses acting on the hull will normally be maximum at the engine room
The bending stresses acting on the hull will normally be maximum at the forward end.
CD0014 — Vessel Struct. Cond..answer: The bending stresses acting on the hull will normally be maximum half way along its length

CD0014 — Vessel Struct. Cond..question: With respect to the ship’s hull, which one of the following statements is most accurate?
options: The main purpose of the transverse frames is to resist bending
Transverse frames are only necessary in shorter vessels
Transverse frames are only necessary in longer vessels
The main purpose of the transverse frames is to resist hydraulic loads
CD0014 — Vessel Struct. Cond..answer: The main purpose of the transverse frames is to resist hydraulic loads

CD0014 — Vessel Struct. Cond..question: With respect to the cross sections of stiffener used for the ship’s hull, which one of the following statements is most accurate?
options: Angle bar has high resistance to twisting
T-profile does not tend to twist and has better resistance to buckling and fatigue than flat bar.
Flat bar performs better in most situations
It is difficult to apply protective coatings to bulb profiles
CD0014 — Vessel Struct. Cond..answer: T-profile does not tend to twist and has better resistance to buckling and fatigue than flat bar.

CD0014 — Vessel Struct. Cond..question: Which one of the following statements about static and dynamic loads on the hull is most accurate?
options: Dynamic loads on the hull can be reduced by slowing down or altering course
Little can be done in heavy weather to reduce the dynamic loads on the hull
Static loads on the hull can be reduced by slowing down or altering course
Slowing down in heavy weather should only be considered in an emergency
CD0014 — Vessel Struct. Cond..answer: Dynamic loads on the hull can be reduced by slowing down or altering course

CD0014 — Vessel Struct. Cond..question: Which one of the following statements about checking the ship’s structure for defects is most accurate?
options: Ship’s crew have insufficient training to inspect the cargo holds, hatch covers and ballast tanks with a view to detecting damage and defects.
Ship’s crew are not allowed to inspect the cargo holds, hatch covers and ballast tanks with a view to detecting damage and defects.
There is no need to detect damage and defects between surveys
Ship’s crew should regularly inspect the cargo holds, hatch covers and ballast tanks with a view to detecting damage and defects
CD0014 — Vessel Struct. Cond..answer: Ship’s crew should regularly inspect the cargo holds, hatch covers and ballast tanks with a view to detecting damage and defects

CD0014 — Vessel Struct. Cond..question: With regard to hull surveys, which one of the following statements is most accurate?
options: The role of ship’s staff should be minimal
Ships staff need to prepare the spaces for entry and have the necessary documentation available
Ships staff only need to prepare the spaces for entry
Ships staff should not be involved.
CD0014 — Vessel Struct. Cond..answer: Ships staff need to prepare the spaces for entry and have the necessary documentation available

CD0014 — Vessel Struct. Cond..question: Which one of these IMO publications requires that Bulk Carriers have a loading instrument?
options: Load line
COLREG
SOLAS
MARPOL
CD0014 — Vessel Struct. Cond..answer: SOLAS

CD0015 — Corrosion Protection I.question: Would cargo remnants, e.g. coal mixed with water affect the corrosion rate?
options: The water in contact with the sulphur in the coal will form an active electrolyte, which will tend to accelerate the corrosion process.
This would have none or little effect on the corrosion rate.
This would have no effect if the water present is fresh water
There will be no corrosion.
CD0015 — Corrosion Protection I.answer: The water in contact with the sulphur in the coal will form an active electrolyte, which will tend to accelerate the corrosion process.

CD0015 — Corrosion Protection I.question: What is the main single factor, which affects the cost of preparation and application to difficult vessel areas?
options: The specialised labour required
The cost of the paint
The cost of access to an area
The Weather condition
CD0015 — Corrosion Protection I.answer: The cost of access to an area

CD0015 — Corrosion Protection I.question: What determines the rate at which the corrosion process of steel proceeds?
options: The amount of oxygen present and the ambient temperature?
The relative sizes of cathodic and anodic areas and the conductivity of the electrolyte?
The conductivity of the electrolyte, ambient temperature, amount of oxygen present and the relative sizes of cathodic and anodic areas?
The Conductivity of the electrolyte.
CD0015 — Corrosion Protection I.answer: The conductivity of the electrolyte, ambient temperature, amount of oxygen present and the relative sizes of cathodic and anodic areas?

CD0015 — Corrosion Protection I.question: Oxygen is usually present where corrosion takes place. What would happen to steel in an area where no oxygen exists?
options: Will corrode in the normal way
It will not corrode
A different form of corrosion could take place
It will be protected against corrosion.
CD0015 — Corrosion Protection I.answer: A different form of corrosion could take place

CD0015 — Corrosion Protection I.question: What are the most important things to monitor when inspecting coating conditions?
options: Inspect the areas only where coating has broken down
Inspect a typical area where you can access easily
Inspect both intact and corroded areas and also inspect angles, corners, behind bars etc.
Inspect suspected areas only.
CD0015 — Corrosion Protection I.answer: Inspect both intact and corroded areas and also inspect angles, corners, behind bars etc.

CD0015 — Corrosion Protection I.question: What is the key role that you carry out when evaluating steel condition?
options: You are there to decide the next repair action
You are there to understand what has happened to the steel
You need to be able to assess the condition and be able to report that condition accurately (so that decisions can be made based on your report.)
You are there to approve the work done.
CD0015 — Corrosion Protection I.answer: You need to be able to assess the condition and be able to report that condition accurately (so that decisions can be made based on your report.)

CD0015 — Corrosion Protection I.question: What type of corrosion on a coated deck-area would you most worry about?
options: 3% scattered corrosion
6% localised corrosion
1% localised pitting corrosion
Localised damage corrosion

CD0015 — Corrosion Protection I.question: What should be observed during application of convertible coating systems in cold weather?
options: That the surface is dry
That sufficient curing time is allowed prior to application of the next coat
That sufficient curing time, above the minimum curing temperature of the coating, is allowed prior to application of the next coat.
The correct ambient temperature.
CD0015 — Corrosion Protection I.answer: That sufficient curing time, above the minimum curing temperature of the coating, is allowed prior to application of the next coat.

CD0015 — Corrosion Protection I.question: What are the most important parameters to be observed during application of a convertible coating system?
options: The absolute number of days stated on over-coating intervals to be observed
The over-coating interval being a product of time and air temperature to be observed
The over-coating interval being a product of time and steel temperature to be observed
To observe the weather condition during the period.
CD0015 — Corrosion Protection I.answer: The over-coating interval being a product of time and steel temperature to be observed

CD0016 — Corrosion Protection II.question: Why should the use of long lines be avoided, if possible, during spray application?
options: Risk of blockages
Risk of pressure drops
Safety risks due to increased length
Risk of paint curing in the line

CD0016 — Corrosion Protection II.question: What is the minimum number of degrees centigrade the steel temperature must be above the dew point before paint application?
Why is fresh water washing important before commencing paint application?
options: To remove oil & grease
To remove corrosion
To remove dust & debris
To remove soluble salts

CD0016 — Corrosion Protection II.question: What piece of equipment would be the most effective in removing corrosion from difficult corners or angled areas?
options: Needle gun
Disc sander
Scraper
Chipping hammer

CD0016 — Corrosion Protection II.question: During a drydock paint application why only check dft’s on spot blasted areas, how do you check the antifouling thickness?
options: You can also check dft’s on non blasted areas
You check the wet film of each coat, at various parts of the hull.
Spot blasted areas are the only areas coated from the steel surface upwards - you control the antifouling thickness by controlling the distribution.
CD0016 — Corrosion Protection II.answer: Spot blasted areas are the only areas coated from the steel surface upwards - you control the antifouling thickness by controlling the distribution.

CD0016 — Corrosion Protection II.question: Paint is applied to a deck in the morning. Each morning the air temperature is 7ºC. In early afternoon the temperature of the air rises to 23ºC. You are told that the maximum overcoating time for the paint coating is 36 hours at 20ºC and 48 hours at 10ºC. In this case, what maximum overcoating time do you allow?
options: You consult the Technical data sheet for the paint
36 hours
48 hours
You consult the paint suppliers representative
24 hours
CD0016 — Corrosion Protection II.answer: You consult the paint suppliers representative

CD0016 — Corrosion Protection II.question: The wet film of paint, which is applied, bears a direct relationship to the final dry film thickness of the coating. Taking wet film measurements can be very important. Why is it important to take these measurements as quickly as possible?
options: To avoid the fresh coat softening the coats underneath leading to possible wrong readings.
So that the painter is disturbed as little as possible.
To obtain as close a reading to the actual wet film as possible.
CD0016 — Corrosion Protection II.answer: To obtain as close a reading to the actual wet film as possible.

CD0016 — Corrosion Protection II.question: The main contaminants in a Marine environment are SALT, CORROSION, MOISTURE, OIL & GREASE, DUST AND HULL FOULING.^M^MWhat is the most efficient method of removing HULL FOULING?
options: Low Pressure High Volume Water Washing.
High Pressure Water Washing.
Scraping to remove the fouling.
Fan Jet Cleaning.

CD0016 — Corrosion Protection II.question: Which of the following statements best describes one of the main advantages of Hydroblasting with fresh water as opposed to Dry Abrasive Blasting?
options: Produces a Surface Profile to aid adhesion of coatings to the surface.
Only requires air power for operation.
As well as removing corrosion products it also removes salt contamination.
The prepared surfaces will flash rust.
CD0016 — Corrosion Protection II.answer: As well as removing corrosion products it also removes salt contamination.

CD0016 — Corrosion Protection II.question: A large area of exposed deck is to be blasted to an agreed standard of SA2 before application of an epoxy paint system. In the vicinity of some pipes where difficult access means that the blasting is not able to remove all the corrosion. What do you do?
options: Reject the whole blasted areas until blasting is redone to the correct SA2 standard.
Accept the blasted areas and go ahead with painting.
Discuss the various options with the contractor.
CD0016 — Corrosion Protection II.answer: Discuss the various options with the contractor.

CD0017 — Steering gear, Operation.question: According to SOLAS, what special steering gear requirement must passenger ships meet that not all other ships require?
options: Each power unit, on its own, must be able to move the rudder from 35° on either side to 30° on the other side in not more than 28 seconds
They must have a main and auxiliary steering gear
There must be oil leakage detection, and for a single failure, steering capability must be regained within 45 seconds
All of the above
CD0017 — Steering gear, Operation.answer: Each power unit, on its own, must be able to move the rudder from 35° on either side to 30° on the other side in not more than 28 seconds

CD0017 — Steering gear, Operation.question: According to the SOLAS rules the rudder should move from 35 degrees one side to 30 degrees on the other side in a maximum of 28 seconds for which one of the following:
options: Only cargo ships above 10,000 tonnes or passenger ships carrying more than 50 passengers
The main steering gear of all ships, other than those with special requirements, such as those with non-conventional steering arrangements
The main and auxiliary steering gear of all ships, other than those with special requirements, such as those with non-conventional steering arrangements
Only oil and chemical tankers and gas carriers
CD0017 — Steering gear, Operation.answer: The main steering gear of all ships, other than those with special requirements, such as those with non-conventional steering arrangements

CD0017 — Steering gear, Operation.question: According to the SOLAS rules, the rudder angle from mid-ships to Port and Starboard should be at least:
options: 65 degrees
35 degrees, or only 25 degrees if a special high efficiency rudder is installed
60 degrees
35 degrees
CD0017 — Steering gear, Operation.answer: 35 degrees

CD0017 — Steering gear, Operation.question: In accordance with SOLAS, when must both steering gear power units be in use?
options: All the time
When the ship is less than four nautical miles from shore
Never, it’s for stand-by use only
In areas where navigation demands special caution
CD0017 — Steering gear, Operation.answer: In areas where navigation demands special caution

CD0017 — Steering gear, Operation.question: The force generated by a steering gear hydraulic system depends on:
options: The hydraulic pressure and the area it acts on
The hydraulic pressure only
The type of incompressible fluid used
The size of the tiller
<![CDATA[]]>
CD0017 — Steering gear, Operation.answer: The hydraulic pressure and the area it acts on

CD0017 — Steering gear, Operation.question: What is the purpose of the rapson slide on a ram type steering gear?
options: It converts the linear movement of the rams into rotation of the tiller
It supports the weight of the rudder stock
It limits the movement of the rudder
It allows the rudder to move vertically
CD0017 — Steering gear, Operation.answer: It converts the linear movement of the rams into rotation of the tiller

CD0017 — Steering gear, Operation.question: Which part of the hydraulic circuit controls the movement of the rudder from port to starboard?
options: The directional valve
The safety valve
The hydraulic pump
The counterbalance valve
CD0017 — Steering gear, Operation.answer: The directional valve

CD0017 — Steering gear, Operation.question: Which one of the following statements best describes the checks carried out during emergency steering drills?
options: All emergency arrangements must be tested including operation from the steering compartment and communication with the bridge.
The checks carried out are the same as those required prior to leaving port, but are more realistic because the ship is moving through the water.
Checks previously carried out prior to leaving port do not need to be repeated, but hand steering from the bridge must be carried out.
In addition to the checks carried out prior to leaving port, hand steering from the bridge must be tested.
CD0017 — Steering gear, Operation.answer: All emergency arrangements must be tested including operation from the steering compartment and communication with the bridge.

CD0017 — Steering gear, Operation.question: Where are remote rudder angle indicators usually fitted?
options: At the bridge steering console and on the bridge wings
In the steering gear compartment only
At the bridge steering console only
In the cargo control room
CD0017 — Steering gear, Operation.answer: At the bridge steering console and on the bridge wings

CD0017 — Steering gear, Operation.question: Which one of these statements best describes the effect of using two steering gear hydraulic pumps instead of one?
options: The speed of rudder movement is greatly increased
The force on the rudder is greatly increased
The speed of rudder movement and the force on the rudder are greatly increased
There is little effect on the speed of movement or the force on the rudder, but reliability is increased
CD0017 — Steering gear, Operation.answer: The speed of rudder movement is greatly increased

CD0017 — Steering gear, Operation.question: Which one of the following is NOT caused by air in a steering gear hydraulic system?
options: Rudder tends to return to mid-ships
Overheating
Corrosion
Erratic movement of the rudder
CD0017 — Steering gear, Operation.answer: Rudder tends to return to mid-ships

CD0017 — Steering gear, Operation.question: Which one of these statements about the force developed by a hydraulic system is true?
options: Force equals pressure times area
Force equals pressure divided by area
Force equals pressure plus area
Pressure equals force times area
CD0017 — Steering gear, Operation.answer: Force equals pressure times area

CD0017 — Steering gear, Operation.question: Which is the only one of the following that is NOT likely to cause overheating of a hydraulic steering gear?
options: Leakage of hydraulic fluid
Air in the main hydraulic system
Pumps running on no-load for long periods of time
High ambient temperatures and blocked oil coolers
CD0017 — Steering gear, Operation.answer: Leakage of hydraulic fluid

CD0017 — Steering gear, Operation.question: When a heavy sea strikes the rudder, which one of these statements best describes what will happen?
options: If the force is large enough, the hydraulic pressure in the steering gear will be high enough to operate the safety valve, and the rudder will move
The rudder is hydraulically locked in position and will not move
The rudder is free to move, but the auto-pilot will bring the ship back on course
The shape and lightweight design of the rudder means that wave forces have no effect
CD0017 — Steering gear, Operation.answer: If the force is large enough, the hydraulic pressure in the steering gear will be high enough to operate the safety valve, and the rudder will move

CD0017 — Steering gear, Operation.question: What special requirement for steering gears is applied to any ship over 70,000 tonnes?
options: The main steering gear must have two or more identical power units
There must be oil leakage detection
There must be automatic change-over in the event of hydraulic leakage
One of the steering gear motors must be supplied from the emergency switchboard
CD0017 — Steering gear, Operation.answer: The main steering gear must have two or more identical power units

CD0017 — Steering gear, Operation.question: Which one of these statements about rudder carrier bearings is true?
options: A separate rudder carrier bearing is only required on ram type steering gears
A rudder carrier bearing is only required on ram type steering gears
A rudder carrier bearing is only required on rotary vane type steering gears
A rudder carrier bearing is not required on rotary vane type steering gears
CD0017 — Steering gear, Operation.answer: A separate rudder carrier bearing is only required on ram type steering gears

CD0017 — Steering gear, Operation.question: According to the SOLAS rules, when must ships fitted with more than one steering gear power unit have at least two of these units running?
options: In all cases, in areas where navigation demands special caution
In areas where navigation demands special caution, unless each individual power unit can perform as a main steering gear
In areas where navigation demands special caution, unless the system is arranged to change over automatically within 45 seconds of a failure to either power unit
When entering or leaving port, or at the discretion of the Master
CD0017 — Steering gear, Operation.answer: In all cases, in areas where navigation demands special caution

CD0017 — Steering gear, Operation.question: Which one of the phrase given in the options most accurately completes the following statement? The ships steering gear must normally be checked and tested by the ship’s crew:
options: Within 12 hours before departure
Within 48 hours before departure
Within 24 hours before departure
Within 72 hours before departure
CD0017 — Steering gear, Operation.answer: Within 12 hours before departure

CD0017 — Steering gear, Operation.question: Which one of the following statements best describes the arrangement of steering gear alarms?
options: Steering gear alarms can only be acknowledged on the bridge, but are indicated elsewhere
Steering gear alarms can be acknowledged on the bridge, or elsewhere
Steering gear alarms are only indicated and acknowledged on the bridge
Steering gear alarms are only indicated and acknowledged in the steering compartment
CD0017 — Steering gear, Operation.answer: Steering gear alarms can only be acknowledged on the bridge, but are indicated elsewhere

CD0017 — Steering gear, Operation.question: Which one of the following statements gives one of the steering gear requirements for passenger ships?
options: Each power unit must be capable of  moving the rudder from 35° on either side to 30° on the other side in not more than 28 seconds
There must be two identical power units which together can move the rudder from 35° on either side to 30° on the other side in not more than 28 seconds
There must be oil leakage detection fitted
The requirements for each steering gear remains the same, even if there is more than one rudder
CD0017 — Steering gear, Operation.answer: Each power unit must be capable of  moving the rudder from 35° on either side to 30° on the other side in not more than 28 seconds

CD0017 — Steering gear, Operation.question: Which one of the phrase given in the options most accurately completes the following statement? A leaking safety valve on a hydraulic steering system is most likely to cause which one of the following:
options: Slow rudder movement
Leakage of oil into drip trays in the steering flat
Excessive hydraulic oil consumption
A time delay before the rudder first starts to move
CD0017 — Steering gear, Operation.answer: Slow rudder movement

CD0017 — Steering gear, Operation.question: Requirements for steering gears are given in which one of the following publications?
options: SOLAS
MARPOL
COLREG
ISM Code
CD0017 — Steering gear, Operation.answer: SOLAS

CD0017 — Steering gear, Operation.question: Which one of the following statements best describes the actions would you take if there is a leak of hydraulic fluid from a steering gear which does not have an automatic change-over system?
options: Isolate the leaking part of the steering gear by following the procedures on the emergency steering instructions
Immediately switch over to another power unit
Immediately switch off all power units
Top up the system oil until repairs can be made
CD0017 — Steering gear, Operation.answer: Isolate the leaking part of the steering gear by following the procedures on the emergency steering instructions

CD0017 — Steering gear, Operation.question: For an electro-hydraulic steering gear, if there is a lot of movement of the wheel in hand steering mode before the steering gear responds, which one of the following best describes the likely causes?
options: Air in the hydraulic control system
Excessive wear in the hydraulic pumps
Loss of one phase of the electrical supply to the pump motor
Overheating of the hydraulic fluid
CD0017 — Steering gear, Operation.answer: Air in the hydraulic control system

CD0017 — Steering gear, Operation.question: Where a steering gear is fitted with oil leak detection what would be the first alarm in the event of loss of oil?
options: Low level alarm in the hydraulic fluid tank
Low level alarm in the hydraulic fluid tank together with stand by pump auto-start
Hydraulic system power failure
Hydraulic system separation
CD0017 — Steering gear, Operation.answer: Low level alarm in the hydraulic fluid tank

CD0017 — Steering gear, Operation.question: For an electro-hydraulic steering gear, if the stand by pump fails to start following a failure of the running pump, which one of the following best describes the likely cause?
options: The pump has not been set to standby or its power supply has been switched off
There has been a significant loss of hydraulic fluid
There is a valve shut somewhere in the system
The starting current has caused overload
CD0017 — Steering gear, Operation.answer: The pump has not been set to standby or its power supply has been switched off

CD0017 — Steering gear, Operation.question: Which one of the phrase given in the options most accurately completes the following statement? The safety valve on a steering gear hydraulic system is most likely to operate because:
options: A heavy sea has hit the rudder
The output pressure from the hydraulic pumps is too high
It has been opened as part of the normal operation of the steering gear
An attempt has been made to put too much helm on, too quickly
CD0017 — Steering gear, Operation.answer: A heavy sea has hit the rudder

CD0017 — Steering gear, Operation.question: Which one of the following statements about steering gear is NOT correct?
options: A main steering gear must be able to move the rudder from 30° on either side to 30° on the other side in less than 28 seconds
A main steering gear must be able to move the rudder from 35° on either side to 35° on the other side
An auxiliary steering gear must be able to move the rudder from 15° on either side to 15° on the other side
Ships with more than one rudder do not need an auxiliary steering gear if they are navigable with one rudder
CD0017 — Steering gear, Operation.answer: A main steering gear must be able to move the rudder from 30° on either side to 30° on the other side in less than 28 seconds

CD0017 — Steering gear, Operation.question: Where is the changeover to local steering carried out?
options: The steering compartment
The bridge
The steering compartment, but it must be acknowledged by the bridge before it can take effect
The engine control room or the bridge
CD0017 — Steering gear, Operation.answer: The steering compartment

CD0017 — Steering gear, Operation.question: Which of the following statements best describes the importance of the purity of the hydraulic oil used in steering gear?
options: Even small solid particles will cause wear, whilst moisture will cause corrosion
Provided the oil remains incompressible, the steering gear will continue to work correctly
Steering gear power actuators are very robust and therefore a degree of oil contamination can be tolerated
Provided the oil viscosity remains within acceptable limits, the steering gear will continue to work correctly
CD0017 — Steering gear, Operation.answer: Even small solid particles will cause wear, whilst moisture will cause corrosion

CD0017 — Steering gear, Operation.question: The steering mode in which the rudder angle is pre-set manually and kept in position automatically, is called?
options: Follow up mode
Auto pilot mode
Non follow up mode
Hand steering mode
CD0017 — Steering gear, Operation.answer: Follow up mode

CD0017 — Steering gear, Operation.question: According to the SOLAS rules the steering gear should be capable of being recharged with hydraulic oil from a fixed storage tank. What is the main reason for this?
options: To ensure that the steering gear can be rapidly recharged with clean hydraulic oil in the event of a leak from the system
To cut down the fire risk and reduce the risk of spillages
Because a steady leakage of oil is to be expected from some steering gears and having a fixed storage tank reduces the time taken for topping up
To ensure that the correct grade of oil is always used
CD0017 — Steering gear, Operation.answer: To ensure that the steering gear can be rapidly recharged with clean hydraulic oil in the event of a leak from the system

CD0017 — Steering gear, Operation.question: Which one of the phrase given in the options most accurately completes the following statement? According to the SOLAS rules, if a ship has more than one rudder and can be manoeuvred with only one rudder, then:
options: Only one main steering gear needs to be fitted to each rudder
Each rudder must be fitted with a main and auxiliary steering gear
An additional main or auxiliary steering gear is only required on each rudder for tankers, chemical tankers and gas carriers above 10,000 tonnes
An additional main or auxiliary steering gear is only required on each rudder for passenger ships of over 70,000 tonnes
CD0017 — Steering gear, Operation.answer: Only one main steering gear needs to be fitted to each rudder

CD0017 — Steering gear, Operation.question: In the event of an oil leak on a steering gear fitted with an automatic change-over system, at what point should the system be automatically split into two?
options: When a main low level alarm operates on either hydraulic oil tank
At the same time as one of the pumps is automatically stopped
When the final low level alarm on either hydraulic oil tank operates
The system will be split into two in the event of any alarm sounding
CD0017 — Steering gear, Operation.answer: When a main low level alarm operates on either hydraulic oil tank

CD0017 — Steering gear, Operation.question: Which is the only one of the following NOT known to have caused moisture to have contaminated the hydraulic oil used for the steering gear?
options: A leaking rudderstock gland
Water collecting on top of hydraulic oil drums stored on deck
Oil for topping up stored in open containers in the steering compartment
Air in the hydraulic control system containing moisture
CD0017 — Steering gear, Operation.answer: A leaking rudderstock gland

CD0017 — Steering gear, Operation.question: Which one of these statements about types of steering gear is true?
options: Higher pressures are needed for the ram type
Higher pressures are needed for the rotary vane type
A greater angle of possible rudder movement is available with ram type steering gears
The ram type takes up less space than the rotary vane type
CD0017 — Steering gear, Operation.answer: Higher pressures are needed for the ram type

CD0017 — Steering gear, Operation.question: According to SOLAS, what special steering gear requirement must tankers above 10,000 tonnes meet that other ships do not require?
options: There must be oil leak detection, and steering capability must be regained within 45 seconds following the loss of one power actuating system
There must be two or more identical power units
Steering capability must be regained within 60 seconds following an oil leak
There must always be full duplication of components up to the rudder stock
CD0017 — Steering gear, Operation.answer: There must be oil leak detection, and steering capability must be regained within 45 seconds following the loss of one power actuating system

CD0017 — Steering gear, Operation.question: If there are no alarms, but the ship stops responding correctly to helm orders, which one of the following best describes the likely causes?
options: A failure in the remote rudder angle indication system
An electrical power failure in the control system
A leaking safety valve
An electrical power failure in the power actuating system
CD0017 — Steering gear, Operation.answer: A failure in the remote rudder angle indication system

CD0017 — Steering gear, Operation.question: What is the most likely cause of the hydraulic lock alarm occurring on a steering gear system?
options: A failure in the control system such as a directional valve sticking open
A failure of one of the hydraulic pumps
Having both hydraulic pumps running at the same time
Failing to purge the system of air
CD0017 — Steering gear, Operation.answer: A failure in the control system such as a directional valve sticking open

CD0017 — Steering gear, Operation.question: What types of valves are actuated in order to move the rudder when local steering is being carried out?
options: Directional valves
Safety valves
Local connecting valves
One way valves
CD0017 — Steering gear, Operation.answer: Directional valves

CD0017 — Steering gear, Operation.question: If the ship suddenly doesn't steer in the direction intended, but no steering gear alarms activate, what is the most likely cause?
options: A failure in the remote rudder angle indication system
An electrical power failure in either the control or actuating system
Air in either the control or actuating hydraulic system
Mechanical failure of a steering gear pump
CD0017 — Steering gear, Operation.answer: A failure in the remote rudder angle indication system

CD0017 — Steering gear, Operation.question: If the rudder will not hold a helm angle in manual or non-follow up mode, which one of the following statements gives the most likely causes?
options: A hydraulic fluid leak in the hydraulic control or power systems
Too high a setting on the safety valve
Air in either the hydraulic control or power systems
Blockage of a directional valve
CD0017 — Steering gear, Operation.answer: A hydraulic fluid leak in the hydraulic control or power systems

CD0017 — Steering gear, Operation.question: Which one of the following would NOT cause slow rudder movement?
options: Air in the hydraulic control system
A leaking safety valve
Partial blocking of a directional valve
Damage to, or partial seizure of, the rudder post or carrier bearing
<![CDATA[ ]]>
CD0017 — Steering gear, Operation.answer: Air in the hydraulic control system

CD0017 — Steering gear, Operation.question: Where a steering gear is fitted with oil leak detection, in the event of loss of oil, what would happen before a second pump automatically started?
options: The low level alarm would need to be acknowledge on the bridge
The hydraulic system would need to be automatically split
The first pump would be stopped automatically
The part of the actuator with leakage, is shut down
CD0017 — Steering gear, Operation.answer: The hydraulic system would need to be automatically split

CD0017 — Steering gear, Operation.question: The ship is at sea and an order to switch over to local steering is given. What knowledge will you need in particular?
options: How to handle emergency situations in general
Knowledge gained from steering the ship in follow up mode from the bridge when entering port
What you have learnt during emergency steering drills and the emergency operating procedures
Detailed knowledge of steering gear construction
CD0017 — Steering gear, Operation.answer: What you have learnt during emergency steering drills and the emergency operating procedures

CD0017 — Steering gear, Operation.question: Where a steering gear is fitted with oil leak detection, in the event of loss of oil, what would the first alarm be, and what would happen?
options: The first low level alarm would be activated, but the pump or pumps that had been running will continue to run
The part of the actuator where the leakage is will be closed down
The pumps would change-over
The part of the actuator without leakage, is shut down
CD0017 — Steering gear, Operation.answer: The first low level alarm would be activated, but the pump or pumps that had been running will continue to run

CD0017 — Steering gear, Operation.question: Which one of the situations described below may cause the need for local steering?
options: Failure on the auto pilot
Failure on one hydraulic pump
Failure on the follow up system
If the bridge is put out of action
CD0017 — Steering gear, Operation.answer: If the bridge is put out of action

CD0017 — Steering gear, Operation.question: Steering gear alarms can only be acknowledged from which one of the following?
options: The steering gear compartment
The engine control room
The wheel house
The duty engineer’s call alarm
CD0017 — Steering gear, Operation.answer: The wheel house

CD0017 — Steering gear, Operation.question: What is the main purpose of the safety valve on a hydraulic steering gear?
options: To protect against leakage between the pressure chambers
To protect the operator
To protect the actuator against too high an oil pressure
To regulate the return flow of oil from the steering gear
CD0017 — Steering gear, Operation.answer: To protect the actuator against too high an oil pressure

CD0017 — Steering gear, Operation.question: The main purpose of emergency steering drills is to:
options: Comply with SOLAS
Check the full function of the steering gear
Make sure that the engineers can perform emergency steering
Make sure that enough of the ship’s crew are trained to carry out emergency steering
CD0017 — Steering gear, Operation.answer: Make sure that enough of the ship’s crew are trained to carry out emergency steering

CD0017 — Steering gear, Operation.question: When in emergency steering mode from the steering flat, how is movement of the steering gear usually created?
options: Start at least one power unit and activate the direction valve
By starting the motors on both power units
By activating the direction valve and the safety valve
By moving the rudder
CD0017 — Steering gear, Operation.answer: Start at least one power unit and activate the direction valve

CD0018 — Cooling Systems.question: Where would you expect to find zinc anodes to be fitted in a diesel engine cooling water system?
options: Inside the end covers of seawater cooled shell and tube type heat exchangers.
On the air side of charge air coolers.
On a plate type heat exchanger using titanium plates.
On the freshwater side of a jacket water cooler.
CD0018 — Cooling Systems.answer: Inside the end covers of seawater cooled shell and tube type heat exchangers.

CD0018 — Cooling Systems.question: What is the main problem associated with using water to cool diesel engine pistons?
options: Risk of leakage into the crankcase.
Specific heat capacity too low.
Risk of cavitation erosion.
Cocktail shaker effect cannot be achieved.
CD0018 — Cooling Systems.answer: Risk of leakage into the crankcase.

CD0018 — Cooling Systems.question: Which of the following equipment is normally cooled by the LT circuit in a central cooling system? There may be more than one correct option.
options: Air compressors.
Diesel engine lubricating oil systems.
Diesel engine cylinder liners and cylinder covers.
Turbochargers.
CD0018 — Cooling Systems.answer: Air compressors.

CD0018 — Cooling Systems.question: How is the flow normally monitored in a piston cooling system?
options: Sight glass and flow alarm in each return line.
Sight glass and flow alarm in each inlet line
Sight glass and flow alarm in the pump inlet.
Sight glass and flow alarm in pump outlet.
CD0018 — Cooling Systems.answer: Sight glass and flow alarm in each return line.

CD0018 — Cooling Systems.question: What is the main reason for including a fresh water generator in the main engine jacket water cooling circuit?
options: To increase the overall plant efficiency.
To allow a smaller jacket water cooler to be fitted.
To reduce the number of pumps fitted.
To help cool the jacket water.
CD0018 — Cooling Systems.answer: To increase the overall plant efficiency.

CD0018 — Cooling Systems.question: At which point does the jacket water normally enter the engine?
options: At the bottom of the liner.
At the cylinder cover.
At the turbocharger.
At the top of the liner.
CD0018 — Cooling Systems.answer: At the bottom of the liner.

CD0018 — Cooling Systems.question: What do you understand by the term primary fluid when referring to diesel engine cooling systems?
options: The coolant that passes through the engine and is cooled in a heat exchanger.
The coolant that passes through the heat exchanger to cool another fluid.
The coolant that is used to preheat the engine.
The fluid that is bled through the fuel injectors.
CD0018 — Cooling Systems.answer: The coolant that passes through the engine and is cooled in a heat exchanger.

CD0018 — Cooling Systems.question: What is the main reason for cooling the charge air supplied by the turbocharger?
options: Increase the density of the air entering the cylinder.
Reduce the temperature of the air entering the cylinder.
Heat up the seawater to feed the fresh water generator.
Reduce the exhaust gas temperature.
CD0018 — Cooling Systems.answer: Increase the density of the air entering the cylinder.

CD0018 — Cooling Systems.question: What is the most common method used for cooling fuel injection valves on large modern heavy fuel oil burning 2 stroke diesel engines?
options: Recirculation of heavy fuel oil.
Direct circulation of freshwater.
Direct circulation of seawater.
Direct circulation of diesel oil.
CD0018 — Cooling Systems.answer: Recirculation of heavy fuel oil.

CD0018 — Cooling Systems.question: What is the purpose of a controller in a cooling water temperature control system?
options: To compare the measured value with the set point and generate an output signal for the control valve actuator.
To measure the temperature of the cooling water system.
To control the flow of the water in the system.
To indicate the control valve position.
CD0018 — Cooling Systems.answer: To compare the measured value with the set point and generate an output signal for the control valve actuator.

CD0018 — Cooling Systems.question: A transducer can be used in a cooling water temperature control system. What do you understand by the term transducer?
options: A device that measures a physical characteristic and generates different physical output.
A device to compare measured value and set point.
A device to measure control valve travel.
A device to boost the controller output signal.
CD0018 — Cooling Systems.answer: A device that measures a physical characteristic and generates different physical output.

CD0018 — Cooling Systems.question: How are the main and bottom end bearings cooled in a diesel engine?
options: Heat is carried away by lubricating oil.
Freshwater cooled.
Air cooled.
Seawater cooled.
CD0018 — Cooling Systems.answer: Heat is carried away by lubricating oil.

CD0018 — Cooling Systems.question: What is the most common type of pump used in a diesel engine jacket water system?
options: Single stage centrifugal pump
Multi stage centrifugal pump
Positive displacement pump
Reciprocating pump
CD0018 — Cooling Systems.answer: Single stage centrifugal pump

CD0018 — Cooling Systems.question: Wax element control valves are often used in diesel engine cooling water systems. How is the valve actuated?
options: Expansion and contraction of the wax element moves the valve.
Water pressure on the wax element moves the valve.
Water flow past the wax element moves the valve.
The temperature of the wax is measured by a sensor which outputs a signal to a controller.
CD0018 — Cooling Systems.answer: Expansion and contraction of the wax element moves the valve.

CD0018 — Cooling Systems.question: In some heat exchangers the tubes are fitted with fins. What is the purpose of these fins?
options: To extend the heat transfer surface.
To strengthen the tubes.
To direct the fluid flow.
To slow down the fluid flow.
CD0018 — Cooling Systems.answer: To extend the heat transfer surface.

CD0018 — Cooling Systems.question: Bore cooling is a common design feature for the main components of a diesel engine. Why is bore cooling used?
options: To allow intense cooling while maintaining component strength.
To make the components lighter.
To prevent corrosion
To prevent scale formation.
CD0018 — Cooling Systems.answer: To allow intense cooling while maintaining component strength.

CD0018 — Cooling Systems.question: The piston rings and liner wall heat up during the operation of the diesel engine. Apart from the combustion process what else causes these components to heat up?
options: Friction
Cylinder lubricating oil
Convection
Jacket water
CD0018 — Cooling Systems.answer: Friction

CD0018 — Cooling Systems.question: How should the jacket water flow through the deaerator?
options: With a rotational flow through the baffles.
Vertically upwards through the baffles.
Vertically downwards through the baffles.
From the center outwards through the baffles.
CD0018 — Cooling Systems.answer: With a rotational flow through the baffles.

CD0018 — Cooling Systems.question: Three way valves used in diesel engine cooling water systems can be arranged as either diverter or mixing valves. What is the normal port arrangement for a mixing valve?
options: Two inlet and one outlet port.
One inlet and two outlet ports.
Three inlet ports.
One inlet, one outlet and a bypass port.
CD0018 — Cooling Systems.answer: Two inlet and one outlet port.

CD0018 — Cooling Systems.question: What is the purpose of the diffuser ring fitted to some centrifugal pumps?
options: To convert the high velocity kinetic energy of the fluid to pressure energy.
To accelerate the fluid in the pump.
It is fitted instead of an impeller.
To help distribute the fluid inside the pump.
