options: Hogged
Sagged
Unstressed
CD0068 — BC Code.answer: Sagged

CD0068 — BC Code.question: Which one of the following identifies what is recommended should be monitored on a bulk carrier that is carrying a cargo of coal?
options: Temperatures, Carbon monoxide and Methane levels
Oxygen levels only
Carbon monoxide levels only
Methane levels prior departure only
CD0068 — BC Code.answer: Temperatures, Carbon monoxide and Methane levels

CD0068 — BC Code.question: Which one of the following statements is the most likely to be true, in relation to a cargo with a high angle of repose of 45°?
options: The cargo pile will be very unstable
The cargo pile will liquefy quickly
The cargo pile will be stable
The cargo pile may produces gases
CD0068 — BC Code.answer: The cargo pile will be stable

CD0068 — BC Code.question: Which one of the following is considered to be the main danger to a bulk carrier in relation to seawater leakage into a cargo space?
options: The cargo is more likely to liquefy
The cargo is likely to be damaged commercially
There is an increased risk of steelwork corrosion
CD0068 — BC Code.answer: The cargo is more likely to liquefy

CD0068 — BC Code.question: Which one of the following identifies the main gases that are likely to be produced by a coal cargo?
options: Oxygen and Methane
Carbon monoxide and Methane
Hydrogen, Oxygen and Carbon monoxide
CD0068 — BC Code.answer: Carbon monoxide and Methane

CD0068 — BC Code.question: A vessel is to load 100,000 tonnes of iron ore with a stowage factor (SF) of 0.50 m³/t. ^M^MWhich one of the given options is the required stowage volume for this cargo?

A vessel is to load 100,000 tonnes of coal with a stowage factor (SF) of 1.50 m³/t.^M^MWhich one of the following will be the required volumetric cargo space to load this cargo, measured in cubic metres, m³?
Which one of the following procedures should be followed when a bulk cargo of coal is being carried at sea?
options: Normal deck safety procedures
Deck area out of use to all crew
Access to deck area only for safety inspections
All hot work and smoking should be prohibited, otherwise normal deck procedures
CD0068 — BC Code.answer: All hot work and smoking should be prohibited, otherwise normal deck procedures

CD0068 — BC Code.question: A cargo of coal appears to be self heating on voyage.^M^MWhich one of the following actions should the ship’s Master take in such circumstances?
options: Continue on voyage
Follow guidance in IMO Bulk Cargo Code and measure carbon monoxide levels
Open hatch covers and spray large quantities of water onto the cargo
Discharge cargo over side
CD0068 — BC Code.answer: Follow guidance in IMO Bulk Cargo Code and measure carbon monoxide levels

CD0068 — BC Code.question: A vessel is to load 20,000 tonnes of iron ore with a stowage factor (SF) of 0.30 m³/t. The vessel has four cargo holds each with a volume of 6,000 m³ and a maximum allowed loading of 7,000 tonnes in each hold. ^M	^MWhich one of the following statements is correct in relation to the above?
options: All four holds will be completely filled with cargo
Each cargo hold will be approximately 50% full by volume
Two holds will be empty and two holds will each be 75% full by weight
All four holds will each be approximately 25% full by volume
CD0068 — BC Code.answer: All four holds will each be approximately 25% full by volume

CD0068 — BC Code.question: Which one of the following statements is the most likely to be true, in relation to a cargo with a low angle of repose of 32°?
options: The cargo pile will be stable
The cargo pile will be very high
The cargo pile may easily shift
The cargo pile will self-heat
CD0068 — BC Code.answer: The cargo pile may easily shift

CD0068 — BC Code.question: Which one of the following identifies how a bulk cargo should generally be loaded in order to reduce the likelihood of the cargo shifting when the ship is rolling heavily in bad weather?
options: Stowed with a high peak at centre of hold
Trimmed and levelled near to the horizontal
Secured with timber
Stowed against hold bulkheads
CD0068 — BC Code.answer: Trimmed and levelled near to the horizontal

CD0068 — BC Code.question: In relation to the classes given in the IMSBC Code, is the following statement true or false?^M^MTwo bulk cargoes, a Class 5.1 dangerous good and a Class 6.2, requiring a category 3 segregation, must have at least 3 metres separating them.
options: True
False
CD0068 — BC Code.answer: False

CD0068 — BC Code.question: In relation to the groups given in the IMSBC Code, is the following statement true or false?^M^MGroup C contains a list of materials which are neither liable to liquefy nor to possess chemical hazards.
options: True
False
CD0068 — BC Code.answer: True

CD0068 — BC Code.question: A bulk cargo may shift within the cargo hold and cause the vessel to list.^M^MWhich one of the following circumstances is this most likely to happen under?
options: The cargo is very dry and the hold is cubically full
The flow moisture point of the cargo is high
The moisture content of the cargo is the same or higher than the flow moisture point of the cargo
The transportable moisture limit is six parts per hundred
CD0068 — BC Code.answer: The moisture content of the cargo is the same or higher than the flow moisture point of the cargo

CD0068 — BC Code.question: A cargo of crushed coal, particle size 1mm and a flow moisture point of 20 is to be loaded. The coal had a moisture content of 17 measured 12 days previously but has lain uncovered on the quayside in heavy rain since.^M^MWhich one of the following actions should the Master of the vessel take?
options: Load the cargo
Refuse to load the cargo and sail
Load only part of the cargo
Request a new test certificate for the moisture content as it should not be more than 7 days old and then decided whether to load
CD0068 — BC Code.answer: Request a new test certificate for the moisture content as it should not be more than 7 days old and then decided whether to load

CD0068 — BC Code.question: A bulk carrier has badly maintained hatch cover seals which allow seawater to leak into the cargo space in bad weather.^M^MWhich one of the following is considered to be the main danger of this situation when considering a non liquefying cargo?
options: The cargo space will fill with water and reserve buoyancy will be lost
The cargo may self-heat
The cargo will produce flammable gas
The cargo will be commercially damaged
CD0068 — BC Code.answer: The cargo space will fill with water and reserve buoyancy will be lost

CD0068 — BC Code.question: Which one of the bulk cargoes given in the options is most likely to be subject to liquefaction?
options: Grains
Steel
Ore concentrates
CD0068 — BC Code.answer: Ore concentrates

CD0068 — BC Code.question: Which one of the following is the main reason why bulk cargo should be trimmed level, or nearly level?
options: To avoid oxygen depletion
To avoid loading an excessive quantity of cargo
To avoid the dangers associated with cargo shifting
CD0068 — BC Code.answer: To avoid the dangers associated with cargo shifting

CD0068 — BC Code.question: Which one of the bulk cargo types given in the options is more likely to have a liquefaction risk?
options: Sand and small stones
Heavy metal ores
Grains such as maize
Scrap steel
CD0068 — BC Code.answer: Heavy metal ores

CD0068 — BC Code.question: A number of deaths have occurred in cargo spaces that have been used for cargoes such as grain and steel scrap (swarf).^M^MWhich one of following is thought to have been absorbed by the cargo, from the cargo space atmosphere, so causing these deaths?
options: Nitrogen
Carbon dioxide
Hydrogen
Oxygen
CD0068 — BC Code.answer: Oxygen

CD0068 — BC Code.question: Is the following statement true or false?^M^MA bulk cargo with low angle of repose has a high likelihood of shifting.
options: True
False
CD0068 — BC Code.answer: True

CD0068 — BC Code.question: Which one of the following statements is the most accurate with regard to actions to be carried out before entry into an enclosed space, such as cargo space, is made?
options: A risk assessment and permit to work must be completed
No specific procedures need to be followed
Log book entries only need to be made
Informing the bridge and the engineroom is the only precaution required
CD0068 — BC Code.answer: A risk assessment and permit to work must be completed

CD0068 — BC Code.question: Which one of the following groups of gases should the atmosphere of an enclosed space, for example a cargo hold, be checked for, before entry is permitted?
options: Oxygen, toxic gases and nitrogen.
Oxygen and carbon dioxide
Toxic gases, oxygen and flammable gas
Argon, nitrogen and flammable gas
CD0068 — BC Code.answer: Toxic gases, oxygen and flammable gas

CD0068 — BC Code.question: Which one of the following is the most likely result of moisture migration in a bulk cargo?
options: A flow state existing on the cargo’s surface
Build up of toxic gases
Oxygen depletion
Self-heating of the cargo
CD0068 — BC Code.answer: A flow state existing on the cargo’s surface

CD0068 — BC Code.question: Which one of the following identifies the action that should be taken with bulk cargoes that may be subject to liquefying?
options: They should never be loaded on a ship
They should only be loaded and carried if the transposable moisture limit is less than 90% of the flow moisture point
They should be allowed to dry out completely before loading
They may be carried without any restriction
CD0068 — BC Code.answer: They should only be loaded and carried if the transposable moisture limit is less than 90% of the flow moisture point

CD0068 — BC Code.question: Which one of the following is the minimum oxygen content that is required before entry into any enclosed space, such as a cargo hold, should be allowed?
Select from the options the phrase which most accurately completes the following statement.^M^M“The angle of repose of a cargo is...
options: ...an indicator that a cargo may go on fire.”
...an indicator that a cargo may become solid."
...an indicator that the cargo may produce flammable gases."
...the natural angle that the cargo pile makes with the horizontal when loaded."
CD0068 — BC Code.answer: ...the natural angle that the cargo pile makes with the horizontal when loaded."

CD0068 — BC Code.question: Which one of the following statements most accurately describes the term ‘moisture migration’?
options: The weight of the cargo.
The angle at which a cargo may start to shift.

The movement of moisture contained in materials by settling and consolidation of the material due to vibration and ship’s motion, which may result in some or all of the materials developing a flow state.
The amount of water in a cargo sample when a flow state may develop.
CD0068 — BC Code.answer: The movement of moisture contained in materials by settling and consolidation of the material due to vibration and ship’s motion, which may result in some or all of the materials developing a flow state.

CD0068 — BC Code.question: A cargo is loaded that has a liquefaction problem and moisture content above the transportable moisture limit.^M^MWhich one of the following effects on the cargo is the most likely result of this situation?
options: Flammable gases will be produced
It will become solid
It will shift in the cargo space
It will self - heat
CD0068 — BC Code.answer: It will shift in the cargo space

CD0068 — BC Code.question: Which one of the following answers is the correct definition for the term ‘stowage factor’?
options: It is the factor, which expresses the number of cubic metres which one tonne of material will occupy.
It is the factor, which expresses the number of square metres which one tonne of material will occupy.
It is the factor, which expresses the relation between liquid cargo and solid cargo.
CD0068 — BC Code.answer: It is the factor, which expresses the number of cubic metres which one tonne of material will occupy.

CD0068 — BC Code.question: Which one of the following answers is the correct definition for the term ‘flow moisture point’?
options: This is the portion of a sample consisting of water, ice or other liquid expressed as a percentage of the total wet mass of that sample.
It is the angle between a horizontal plane and the cone slope of such material.
This is the percentage moisture content at which a flow state develops under the prescribed method of test.
CD0068 — BC Code.answer: This is the percentage moisture content at which a flow state develops under the prescribed method of test.

CD0068 — BC Code.question: Which one of the following answers is the correct definition for the term ‘transportable moisture content’ (TML)?
options: This represents the maximum moisture content of the material which is considered safe for carriage in ships which are not specially designed for the purpose.
This is the factor, which expresses the number of square metres which one tonne of material will occupy.
It is the factor, which expresses the relation between liquid cargo and solid cargo.
CD0068 — BC Code.answer: This represents the maximum moisture content of the material which is considered safe for carriage in ships which are not specially designed for the purpose.

CD0068 — BC Code.question: Which one of the following is the main reason that water should not be used to extinguish fire in the cargo hold while at sea?
options: It may cause damage to the cargo.
It may cause damage to the hull of the ship.
It may bring the moisture content of the cargo material to a flow state.
CD0068 — BC Code.answer: It may bring the moisture content of the cargo material to a flow state.

CD0068 — BC Code.question: In which one of the following would you normally find information about the maximum loading weight of each cargo hold?
options: On the ships fire plan
In the ship’s loading manual and on the ships capacity plan
In the ship’s SMS manual
CD0068 — BC Code.answer: In the ship’s loading manual and on the ships capacity plan

CD0068 — BC Code.question: In which one of the following would you normally find the two common methods of determining the angle of repose?
options: In the IMSBC Code, Appendix 1
In the IMSBC Code, Section 8 and Appendix 2
In the BLU Manual of the IMSBC Code supplements
CD0068 — BC Code.answer: In the IMSBC Code, Section 8 and Appendix 2

CD0068 — BC Code.question: Which one of the following terms is the acronym “TML” used for in the IMSBC Code?
options: Transportable moisture limit
Threshold maximum limit
Transportation minimum level
CD0068 — BC Code.answer: Transportable moisture limit

CD0069 — Basic Refrigeration Theory.question: 0 Kelvin is equal to .....?
options: 0 Fahrenheit
0 ˚Celsius
–273,16 ˚Celsius
+ 273,16 ˚Celsius

CD0069 — Basic Refrigeration Theory.question: What is the saturation temperature?
options: The temperature at which a fluid boils or condenses, it varies with pressure.
The temperature at which a fluid boils or condenses, it is independent of pressure.
It is the point where the ice starts to melt.
It is the same as critical point for a gas.
CD0069 — Basic Refrigeration Theory.answer: The temperature at which a fluid boils or condenses, it varies with pressure.

CD0069 — Basic Refrigeration Theory.question: What is absolute pressure?
options: It is the same as 100% vacuum.
Atmospheric pressure plus gauge pressure.
It is equal to atmospheric pressure.
It is the same as gauge pressure.

CD0069 — Basic Refrigeration Theory.question: What is the main problem with Carbon dioxide as a refrigerant?
options: Extremely inflammable.
Extremely low working pressure.
Extremely high cost.
Extremely high working pressure.

CD0069 — Basic Refrigeration Theory.question: What are the disadvantages of ammonia as a refrigerant?
options: It is toxic and inflammable.
It is very expensive.
It can only be used on very large refrigeration systems.
It cannot be used in refrigeration systems with screw compressor.

CD0069 — Basic Refrigeration Theory.question: If a running system regularly requires charge of refrigerant, what should be done?
options: Find the leak and rectify the problem before the system is charged.
Charge the system, modern refrigerants are cheap and do not harm the environment.
Charge the system, find the leak and rectify the problem.
Replace the lost refrigerant with nitrogen.
CD0069 — Basic Refrigeration Theory.answer: Find the leak and rectify the problem before the system is charged.

CD0069 — Basic Refrigeration Theory.question: What will be an adequate allowance for oil circulation in a refrigeration system?
options: One litre of oil for every thirty kilo of refrigerant charge.
One litre of oil for every twenty kilo of refrigerant charge.
One litre of oil for every kilo of refrigerant charge.
One litre of oil for every two kilo of refrigerant charge.
CD0069 — Basic Refrigeration Theory.answer: One litre of oil for every twenty kilo of refrigerant charge.

CD0069 — Basic Refrigeration Theory.question: The ideal temperature of a freeze room is:
options: 0°C to -5°C

CD0069 — Basic Refrigeration Theory.question: The term “specific enthalpy” of a fluid, measured in kJ/kg, is used to quantify the energy per unit mass due to ……………?
options: the internal energy.
the sum of the internal energy plus the volume.
the sum of the pressure plus the volume.
the sum of the internal energy plus the product of the pressure and volume.
CD0069 — Basic Refrigeration Theory.answer: the sum of the internal energy plus the product of the pressure and volume.

CD0069 — Basic Refrigeration Theory.question: What is the disadvantage of the manually operated expansion valve?
options: It can only be used with modern refrigerants.
It responds to quickly to changes in load.
It cannot be used with modern refrigerants.
It is unresponsive to changes in load.
CD0069 — Basic Refrigeration Theory.answer: It is unresponsive to changes in load.

CD0069 — Basic Refrigeration Theory.question: The operation of the thermostatic expansion valve is based on?
options: Constant degree of superheat in the vapour at the evaporator.
Constant flow of refrigeration medium.
Constant evaporator pressure.
Constant temperature in the condenser.
CD0069 — Basic Refrigeration Theory.answer: Constant degree of superheat in the vapour at the evaporator.

CD0069 — Basic Refrigeration Theory.question: The closed cycle refrigeration system works on the principle of which of the following?
options: Rapid expansion and loss of refrigerant.
Rapid expansion and recirculation of the refrigerant.
Vapour compression with loss of refrigerant.
Vapour compression and recirculation of the refrigerant.
CD0069 — Basic Refrigeration Theory.answer: Vapour compression and recirculation of the refrigerant.

CD0069 — Basic Refrigeration Theory.question: The operation of the automatic expansion valve is based on?
options: Constant evaporator pressure and temperature.
Constant evaporator pressure.
Constant evaporator temperature.
Constant flow of refrigeration medium.

CD0069 — Basic Refrigeration Theory.question: When the desired cold room temperature is reached in a refrigeration system operating on the direct expansion principle, which of the following shuts off the evaporator for the room?
options: Thermostatically controlled expansion valve.
Low pressure cut out.
High pressure cut out.
Solenoid valve operated by thermostatic switch.
CD0069 — Basic Refrigeration Theory.answer: Solenoid valve operated by thermostatic switch.

CD0069 — Basic Refrigeration Theory.question: Put in the correct words.^MAccording to the second law of thermodynamics heat can only transfer naturally from a region of high temperature to a region of ………………….unless mechanical work is done on the system
options: high pressure
low temperature
equal temperature

CD0069 — Basic Refrigeration Theory.question: During automatic operation of a refrigeration system the starting and stopping of the compressor is usually achieved by which of the following?
options: Low pressure cut out.
Thermostatic switch.
Temperature in the cold room.
Manual on/off switch.

CD0069 — Basic Refrigeration Theory.question: Which of the following does the term latent heat describe when referring to a refrigerant?
options: The temperature.
Heat required to cause evaporation at constant boiling temperature and pressure.
The heat required to superheat the refrigerant gas.
The heat required to raise the liquid temperature to boiling point.
CD0069 — Basic Refrigeration Theory.answer: Heat required to cause evaporation at constant boiling temperature and pressure.

CD0069 — Basic Refrigeration Theory.question: What are the main components in a closed refrigeration cycle?
options: Compressor, condenser, expansion valve and receiver.
Compressor, condenser, expansion valve and evaporator.
Compressor, oil separator, expansion valve and evaporator.
Compressor, condenser and evaporator.
CD0069 — Basic Refrigeration Theory.answer: Compressor, condenser, expansion valve and evaporator.

CD0069 — Basic Refrigeration Theory.question: To be able to evaporate a medium at –20˚C and to condense the same medium at +30˚C we have to ........
options: increase the pressure
decrease the pressure

CD0070 — Food Handling.question: When requisitioning stores and provisions, how can shipping companies secure practical cooperation from their suppliers?
options: By requiring them to provide, wherever possible, packaging best suited to subsequent handling and disposal by the vessel.
By making it a condition of contract that the supplier receives and disposes of all garbage that a ship lands in the port of supply.
By requiring that no plastic is used in any goods and provisions supplied to the vessel.
CD0070 — Food Handling.answer: By requiring them to provide, wherever possible, packaging best suited to subsequent handling and disposal by the vessel.

CD0070 — Food Handling.question: Under Annex V of MARPOL 73/78, at what distance from shore may a vessel outside a Special Area dispose of paper, rags and glass bottles that have been ground down or comminuted into the sea?
options: > 3 miles.
> 12 miles.
> 25 miles.
Disposal to sea is prohibited.
CD0070 — Food Handling.answer: > 3 miles.

CD0070 — Food Handling.question: For preference and if possible, how should the amount of garbage be estimated for the purposes of the entries in the Garbage Record Book?
options: Cubic metres by category.
Metric tones overall per operation.
US gallons per category.
Number of standard garbage bags.
Kilograms per package.
CD0070 — Food Handling.answer: Cubic metres by category.

CD0070 — Food Handling.question: Which ships are required to carry a Garbage Management Plan?
options: All ships of 400 gross tonnage and above and every ship certified to carry 15 persons or more.
All ships of 500 tonnes or more and with a keel laid after 1st January 1998.
All ships with a crew of 15 persons or more.
All passenger ships not fitted with an approved incinerator device.
CD0070 — Food Handling.answer: All ships of 400 gross tonnage and above and every ship certified to carry 15 persons or more.

CD0070 — Food Handling.question: Under Annex V of MARPOL 73/78, at what distance from shore may a vessel inside a Special Area dispose of cooked food waste that has been ground down or comminuted into the sea?
options: > 12 miles.
Disposal to sea is prohibited.
> 3 miles.
> 25 miles.
CD0070 — Food Handling.answer: > 12 miles.

CD0070 — Food Handling.question: Should the Master obtain a receipt or certificate for garbage landed to a port reception facility and why?
options: Yes, because it confirms and cross-references with the corresponding entry in the Garbage Record Book.
No, it is not necessary to obtain a receipt, or make an entry in a Garbage Record Book when garbage is landed to an official Port Reception Facility.
No, because the entry in the Garbage Record Book gives all the necessary information.
Yes, because it is a requirement under the ISPS Code.
CD0070 — Food Handling.answer: Yes, because it confirms and cross-references with the corresponding entry in the Garbage Record Book.

CD0070 — Food Handling.question: Will the entries in a Garbage Record Book only ever be used to convict a vessel’s Master and crew in the event of a pollution incident?
options: No – a Garbage Record Book can be used to demonstrate that a vessel is complying with requirements and can be used to eliminate a vessel from an inquiry or absolve her of blame in the event of a suspected pollution incident.
A Garbage Record Book cannot be used either to convict or protect a vessel’s Master and crew in relation to alleged pollution.
Yes – a Garbage Record Book is only admissible as prosecuting evidence.
CD0070 — Food Handling.answer: No – a Garbage Record Book can be used to demonstrate that a vessel is complying with requirements and can be used to eliminate a vessel from an inquiry or absolve her of blame in the event of a suspected pollution incident.

CD0070 — Food Handling.question: In specific relation to MARPOL 73/78, can a Port State Control officer board and inspect a foreign-flagged vessel?
options: Yes.
No.
CD0070 — Food Handling.answer: Yes.

CD0070 — Food Handling.question: How long is it estimated that it will take for a tin can to degrade in the sea?
options: 100 years.
1 year.
14 months.
450 years.
CD0070 — Food Handling.answer: 100 years.

CD0070 — Food Handling.question: Annex V to MARPOL 73/78 refers to a specific area of waste management. Which of the following is it?
options: The handling of those types of food, domestic and operational waste generated during the normal running of a vessel and liable to be disposed of continuously or periodically.
The standards on packing, marking, labelling, documentation, stowage, quantity limitations, exceptions and notifications for preventing pollution by harmful substances.
The processing of those types of operational waste generated as a result of cargo and ballast operations.
CD0070 — Food Handling.answer: The handling of those types of food, domestic and operational waste generated during the normal running of a vessel and liable to be disposed of continuously or periodically.

CD0070 — Food Handling.question: Under Annex V of MARPOL 73/78, at what distance from shore may a vessel inside a Special Area dispose of paper, rags and glass bottles that have been ground down or comminuted into the sea?
options: Disposal to sea is prohibited.
> 3 miles.
> 12 miles.
> 25 miles.
CD0070 — Food Handling.answer: Disposal to sea is prohibited.

CD0070 — Food Handling.question: In order to meet the definition of “comminuted waste” under Annex V to MARPOL 73/78, what size of mesh must the particles be able to pass through?
options: 25 mm.
30 mm.
10 mm.
50 mm.
CD0070 — Food Handling.answer: 25 mm.

CD0070 — Food Handling.question: You are taking stores in port. A ship’s officer and a port official approach and say they wish to look inside some of the packages. Under which Code are they required to carry out such inspections?
options: The International Ship and Port Facility Security (ISPS) Code.
MARPOL 73/78.
The International Health and Safety (Ships Provisions) Regulations.
The World Health Organization Foodstuffs Monitoring Guidelines.
CD0070 — Food Handling.answer: The International Ship and Port Facility Security (ISPS) Code.

CD0070 — Food Handling.question: Which international regulations deal specifically with the prevention of pollution by garbage from ships?
options: Annex V, MARPOL 73/78
Chapter II, SOLAS 1974
Annex I, ISPS Code.
Section III, ISPS Code.
Annex VII, MARPOL 73/78
Chapter VI, SOLAS 1974.
CD0070 — Food Handling.answer: Annex V, MARPOL 73/78

CD0070 — Food Handling.question: The United States Centers for Disease Control and Prevention run a program designed to protect passenger and crew health by minimizing the risk of gastrointestinal illness aboard cruise ships. What is it called?
options: The Vessel Sanitation Program.
The Cruise Ship Health Monitoring System.
The Cruise Industry Best Practise in Passenger Health Scheme.
The Homeland Security (Food Terrorism) Program.
CD0070 — Food Handling.answer: The Vessel Sanitation Program.

CD0070 — Food Handling.question: How should wooden cutting boards be arranged after washing?
options: They should be stacked in such a way that air circulates over all surfaces during drying.
They should be roughly wiped with a drying cloth and stacked one on top of another.
They should be placed in a dishwasher, which is programmed on the “accelerated drying” cycle.
They should be rested on the galley range with the plate on minimum heat, until dry to the touch.
Wooden cutting boards should only ever be scraped, sprayed with a sanitizer spray and wiped dry; they should never be washed with water.
CD0070 — Food Handling.answer: They should be stacked in such a way that air circulates over all surfaces during drying.

CD0070 — Food Handling.question: Which of the following is the recommended form of footwear for the galley?
options: B.
D.
A.
C.
CD0070 — Food Handling.answer: B.

CD0070 — Food Handling.question: Is smoking permitted in the galley?  (Select the most correct answer).
options: No.
Yes.
Yes, but only when the serving of food is complete.
Yes, but only between the hours of 2000 and 0600.
No if the vessel is in port, yes if it is at sea.
CD0070 — Food Handling.answer: No.

CD0070 — Food Handling.question: Is staphylococcal food poisoning spread directly from person-to-person?  (Select the most correct answer).
options: No.
Yes.
Yes, but only where the carrier has suffered from an infectious food poisoning virus within the previous 3 months.
Generally no, although there is a remote possibility if the average temperature in the galley does not drop below 22.7°C throughout the working day.
CD0070 — Food Handling.answer: No.

CD0070 — Food Handling.question: A steward reaches into a sink of soapy water to release the plug and cuts his hand on a knife lying in the bottom. Which of the following policies would have been most effective in avoiding this accident, while still following a practical and hygienic approach to the cleanliness of the equipment?
options: Every person washes their own knives.
Detergent is not used when washing knives.
There is a dedicated sink for washing knives.
There is a dedicated time for washing knives.
Heavy-duty kitchen gloves are used when washing knives and other utensils.
CD0070 — Food Handling.answer: Every person washes their own knives.

CD0070 — Food Handling.question: What kind of saw is used to cut bone that is deep and well covered by meat?
options: A bow saw.
A bone saw.
A tenon saw.
A tendon saw.
A gullet saw.
A rake saw.
CD0070 — Food Handling.answer: A bow saw.

CD0070 — Food Handling.question: It is recommended that personnel engaged in food handling should avoid using perfume and scented anti-perspirant body sprays. Why is this?
options: Because there is a possibility that the scent can transfer to food during handling.
Because the heat of the galley will react with the alcohol in the perfume and intoxicate the wearer.
Because the heat of the galley will react with the perfume and induce itching.
Because the heat of the galley area will increase the evaporation of the scent and mask the aroma from the food.
CD0070 — Food Handling.answer: Because there is a possibility that the scent can transfer to food during handling.

CD0070 — Food Handling.question: What is the best policy to follow, in order to prevent personnel from other departments introducing germs and other forms of contamination into the galley?
options: Prohibit unauthorized persons from the galley and storeroom areas at all times.
Only permit other persons to enter between the hours of 2000 and 0600.
Post a notice outside the galley access door requesting personnel to knock before entering, so that you can check them prior to granting permission.
Require all visitors to the galley to pass through a designated decontamination area on entering.
CD0070 — Food Handling.answer: Prohibit unauthorized persons from the galley and storeroom areas at all times.

CD0070 — Food Handling.question: Some fresh prawns have been peeled in preparation for a cocktail dish. Some fresh salad has been cleaned and prepared to accompany it. The dish is not required for another four hours. What will you do with these ingredients in the meantime?
options: The prawns and the salad will be placed in separate containers, covered and refrigerated until required.
The prawns will be refrigerated and the salad left in cold water to keep it fresh.
The prawns and salad will be placed in separate dishes, covered in tin foil and left on the workbench until required.

CD0070 — Food Handling.question: You have just collected provisions from the freezers and the dry store room and are returning up the stairway to the galley. options: I will report the accident to my superior and ensure that an entry is made in the galley accident logbook in compliance with the company safety policy. CD0092 — Introduction to MARPOL.question: Which one of the following best sums up the general principle of MARPOL Annex V for discharging garbage into the sea?
options: Any discharges should be as far as practicable from nearest land
Any discharges should be as near as possible to land
All garbage should be burnt before discharge into the sea
All garbage should be chopped into small pieces before discharge
Incorrect
Correct
CD0092 — Introduction to MARPOL.answer: Any discharges should be as far as practicable from nearest land

CD0092 — Introduction to MARPOL.question: When garbage is in the sea marine animals can be killed. Which one of the following best explains how garbage kills them?
options: They eat some kinds of garbage
The garbage blocks their view of their food
They can hit their heads on floating garbage
The garbage can block the sunlight
Incorrect
Correct
CD0092 — Introduction to MARPOL.answer: They eat some kinds of garbage

CD0092 — Introduction to MARPOL.question: A barge collects your ship’s garbage while it is in port. Every day the barge gives you a receipt for the garbage. Which one of the following is the best thing to do with the receipts?
options: Keep them in the Garbage Record Book
Keep them in the Oil Record Book
Put them in the paper recycling bin
Keep them with the bunker receipts
Incorrect
Correct
CD0092 — Introduction to MARPOL.answer: Keep them in the Garbage Record Book

CD0092 — Introduction to MARPOL.question: What are the MARPOL Annex IV requirements for records on ships which do not treat sewage?
options: There are no requirements to maintain records
The sewage holding tank level is to be recorded daily
The sewage holding tank level is to be recorded weekly
The sewage holding tank level is to be recorded at the end of every voyage
Incorrect
Correct
CD0092 — Introduction to MARPOL.answer: There are no requirements to maintain records

CD0092 — Introduction to MARPOL.question: If a ship has an approved sewage treatment plant in use, how far from land must it be before it is allowed to discharge overboard, according to MARPOL Annex IV?
options: Any distance
At least 12 miles
At least 3 miles
At least 50 miles
Incorrect
Correct
CD0092 — Introduction to MARPOL.answer: Any distance

CD0092 — Introduction to MARPOL.question: When the MARPOL Convention entered into force the annexes on pollution from sewage, garbage and harmful substances in packaged form were voluntary.^MWhich one of the following is the most likely reason for them later becoming mandatory?
options: Growing worldwide recognition of pollution of the types regulated by those annexes
The wrecking of the oil tanker Torrey Canyon
Another convention regulating sewage, garbage and harmful substances in packaged form was revoked
IMO inspectors insisted on them becoming mandatory
Incorrect
Correct
CD0092 — Introduction to MARPOL.answer: Growing worldwide recognition of pollution of the types regulated by those annexes

CD0092 — Introduction to MARPOL.question: Which one of the following was the main reason for the public concern that led to the MARPOL Convention?
options: There was increasing marine pollution due to the increasing number and size of ships
The International Maritime Organisation (IMO) was created
The United Nations was created
Global warming was discovered
Incorrect
Correct
CD0092 — Introduction to MARPOL.answer: There was increasing marine pollution due to the increasing number and size of ships

CD0092 — Introduction to MARPOL.question: The MARPOL Convention brought in rules in Annex II to reduce chemical pollution of the sea.^MWhich one of the following is the most likely reason for chemical pollution of the sea becoming a problem?
options: Increasing volumes of chemicals and their regular carriage on ships
The wrecking of the oil tanker Torrey Canyon
More types of chemicals were being made
The sea sometimes became acid
Incorrect
Correct
CD0092 — Introduction to MARPOL.answer: Increasing volumes of chemicals and their regular carriage on ships

CD0092 — Introduction to MARPOL.question: Which one of the given options would be the best action to take following an incident where leaking oil polluted the water around your ship?
options: Contain the oil with booms
Spray oil dispersant as soon as possible
Throw rags on the oil
Set fire to the oil
Incorrect
Correct
CD0092 — Introduction to MARPOL.answer: Contain the oil with booms

CD0092 — Introduction to MARPOL.question: Which one of the following best describes the main goal of MARPOL Annex III?
options: To reduce the harm to the environment from harmful substances in packaged form
To reduce the amount of harmful substances in the sea
To reduce the amount of dumping into the sea
To make the clean up of harmful substances in packaged form in the sea easier
Incorrect
Correct
CD0092 — Introduction to MARPOL.answer: To reduce the harm to the environment from harmful substances in packaged form

CD0092 — Introduction to MARPOL.question: Which one of the following best describes the requirement in MARPOL Annex VI intended to minimise accidental emissions of Sulphur Oxides (SOx) inside Sulphur Emission Control Areas (SECAs)?
options: Requiring a written fuel changeover procedure
Requiring separate high and low sulphur fuel day tanks
Requiring sulphur meters in exhaust pipes
Requiring a bunker sample be kept on board
Incorrect
Correct
CD0092 — Introduction to MARPOL.answer: Requiring a written fuel changeover procedure

CD0092 — Introduction to MARPOL.question: The MARPOL convention requires ships to report pollution incidents. Which one of the following is the main reason for this?
options: So that action can be taken to clean up the pollution
So that someone can be prosecuted
So that ships can be blacklisted by ports
So that insurance companies can put up premiums
Incorrect
Correct
CD0092 — Introduction to MARPOL.answer: So that action can be taken to clean up the pollution

CD0092 — Introduction to MARPOL.question: Which one of the following most closely matches the definition of ‘garbage’ in MARPOL Annex V?
options: All kinds of food, domestic and operational waste
All kinds of food and domestic waste
All solid waste produced by the ship
Solid waste and packages containing liquid waste produced by the ship
Incorrect
Correct
CD0092 — Introduction to MARPOL.answer: All kinds of food, domestic and operational waste

CD0092 — Introduction to MARPOL.question: Which one of the following best matches the MARPOL Annex II definition of a “noxious liquid substance”?
options: Any substance listed as pollution category X, Y or Z in the International Bulk Chemical Code
Any oil not listed in MARPOL Annex I
Any substance listed in the IMDG Code
Any substance which could kill a human within 12 hours
Incorrect
Correct
CD0092 — Introduction to MARPOL.answer: Any substance listed as pollution category X, Y or Z in the International Bulk Chemical Code

CD0092 — Introduction to MARPOL.question: Which one of the following best describes how coastal states can find out if a sinking ship is carrying MARPOL Annex III cargo?
options: A manifest listing the harmful substances must be left ashore
The SMPEP will require the Mayday broadcast to say that harmful substances are on board
The ship’s AIS will broadcast the list of harmful substances on board
A red flag is to be flown while harmful substances are on board
Incorrect
Correct
CD0092 — Introduction to MARPOL.answer: A manifest listing the harmful substances must be left ashore

CD0092 — Introduction to MARPOL.question: Which one of the following best describes the requirement in MARPOL Annex VI intended to minimise operational emissions of CO2?
options: All ships are required to have a Ship Energy Efficiency Management Plan
Only new ships will be required to have a Ship Energy Efficiency Management Plan
New ships will have to go slower than old ships
All ships will have to reduce speed by 10%
Incorrect
Correct
CD0092 — Introduction to MARPOL.answer: All ships are required to have a Ship Energy Efficiency Management Plan

CD0092 — Introduction to MARPOL.question: Which one of the following best describes the requirement in MARPOL Annex VI intended to minimise operational emissions of Ozone Depleting Substances (ODS)?
options: Emissions during maintenance are banned and gases must be recaptured for recycling
Equipment containing ODS must be maintenance free
Fire extinguishers must not be serviced
All types of ODS must be removed from the ship by 2012
Incorrect
Correct
CD0092 — Introduction to MARPOL.answer: Emissions during maintenance are banned and gases must be recaptured for recycling

CD0092 — Introduction to MARPOL.question: Which one of the following best describes the way that sewage can damage the marine environment?
options: It can contain bacteria, parasites and viruses
It can block out the sunlight
It can cover the seabed
It can increase oxygen levels in the water
Incorrect
Correct
CD0092 — Introduction to MARPOL.answer: It can contain bacteria, parasites and viruses

CD0092 — Introduction to MARPOL.question: Which one of the following kinds of garbage does MARPOL Annex V allow to be discharged overboard while the ship is inside a special area?
options: Food
Cargo residues
Paper
Wood
Incorrect
Correct
CD0092 — Introduction to MARPOL.answer: Food

CD0092 — Introduction to MARPOL.question: Which one of the following most closely matches the definition of ‘oil’ in MARPOL Annex I?
options: Any oil from petroleum
Unrefined (crude) oil
Any oil that floats on water
Any oil that burns in air
Incorrect
Correct
CD0092 — Introduction to MARPOL.answer: Any oil from petroleum

CD0092 — Introduction to MARPOL.question: Which one of the following best describes the records of noxious liquid operations that ships have to maintain to satisfy MARPOL Annex II?
options: A cargo record book must be completed after any transfer of cargo or ballasting of cargo tanks
The oil record book Part II must be completed after cargo operations
A record book must be completed only after cargo operations
A record book must be completed only after cargo tank washing operations
Incorrect
Correct
CD0092 — Introduction to MARPOL.answer: A cargo record book must be completed after any transfer of cargo or ballasting of cargo tanks

CD0092 — Introduction to MARPOL.question: Which one of the following best describes the purpose of the slop tank that MARPOL Annex I requires oil tankers to be fitted with?
options: To ensure tank washings can settle before the water is discharged overboard
To heat water for tank washing
To store oil for crude oil washing
To heat oil for crude oil washing
Incorrect
Correct
CD0092 — Introduction to MARPOL.answer: To ensure tank washings can settle before the water is discharged overboard

CD0092 — Introduction to MARPOL.question: Which one of the following describes the most common way that the substances regulated by MARPOL Annex III cause harm to the marine environment?
options: They are poisonous
They spread across the surface of the water
They cover the sea bed
They cannot be seen
Incorrect
Correct
CD0092 — Introduction to MARPOL.answer: They are poisonous

CD0092 — Introduction to MARPOL.question: Select the option which is the reason why MARPOL Annex I requires most crude oil tankers to have cargo oil piping designed to minimise oil retention.
options: To reduce the amount of oil in the slop tank
To reduce the corrosion in the pipes
To reduce the pollution when the cargo tank is ballasted
To reduce the risk of capsize while in ballast
Incorrect
Correct
CD0092 — Introduction to MARPOL.answer: To reduce the amount of oil in the slop tank

CD0092 — Introduction to MARPOL.question: Which one of the following best describes the main goal of MARPOL Annex VI?
options: To reduce the harm to the environment from air pollution from ships
To ban the emissions of air pollutants from ships
To capture emissions of air pollutants from ships
To reduce the harm to the environment from oil pollution from ships
Incorrect
Correct
CD0092 — Introduction to MARPOL.answer: To reduce the harm to the environment from air pollution from ships

CD0092 — Introduction to MARPOL.question: Which one of the following best describes the main purpose of the SOPEP required by MARPOL Annex I?
options: To describe the actions to be taken to reduce the discharge of oil following an accident
To act as a telephone directory
To record the actions taken following an accidental discharge of oil
To describe the actions needed to evacuate the ship while surrounded by oil
Incorrect
Correct
CD0092 — Introduction to MARPOL.answer: To describe the actions to be taken to reduce the discharge of oil following an accident

CD0092 — Introduction to MARPOL.question: Which one of the following best describes the means required by MARPOL Annex IV to reduce accidental discharges of sewage?
options: Holding tanks must have a means to indicate visually the amount of its contents
Holding tanks must be in a protective location away from the hull
Sewage treatment plants must be fitted with an alarm on the outlet pipe
Sewage comminuting and disinfecting systems must have a disinfectant low level alarm
Incorrect
Correct
CD0092 — Introduction to MARPOL.answer: Holding tanks must have a means to indicate visually the amount of its contents

CD0092 — Introduction to MARPOL.question: Which one of the following is the most likely way in which a noxious liquid substance could harm marine plants?
options: By blocking the sunlight
By making the leaves slippery
By changing the water colour
By making the rocks slippery
Incorrect
Correct
CD0092 — Introduction to MARPOL.answer: By blocking the sunlight

CD0092 — Introduction to MARPOL.question: Which one of the following documents is required by MARPOL Annex II in order to minimise the harm caused by an accidental discharge of noxious liquids?
options: A Shipboard Marine Pollution Emergency Plan
A Noxious Liquids Cargo Record Book
A Procedures and Arrangements Manual
A Safety Management System
Incorrect
Correct
CD0092 — Introduction to MARPOL.answer: A Shipboard Marine Pollution Emergency Plan

CD0092 — Introduction to MARPOL.question: Which one of the following best describes the requirements of MARPOL Annex V for plastic garbage?
options: It must be discharged ashore, even after incineration
It must be discharged ashore or incinerated
It must be incinerated at high temperatures
It can only be discharged outside a special area
Incorrect
Correct
CD0092 — Introduction to MARPOL.answer: It must be discharged ashore, even after incineration

CD0092 — Introduction to MARPOL.question: Under MARPOL Annex III what operational discharges of harmful substances in packaged form are allowed?
options: Discharge of leakages might be allowed by the flag state
Damaged packages can be discharged overboard
None
None, unless via the bilge separator
Incorrect
Correct
CD0092 — Introduction to MARPOL.answer: Discharge of leakages might be allowed by the flag state

CD0092 — Introduction to MARPOL.question: Which one of the following is a kind of environmental damage caused by air pollutants regulated by MARPOL Annex VI?
options: Acid rain
Heavy rain
Drought
Lightning strikes
Incorrect
Correct
CD0092 — Introduction to MARPOL.answer: Acid rain

CD0092 — Introduction to MARPOL.question: Which one of the following best describes the purpose of the placards required on some ships by MARPOL Annex V?
options: They show the garbage disposal requirements.
They show the garbage collection areas
They show the garbage disposal positions
They show the penalties for illegal garbage discharges
Incorrect
Correct
CD0092 — Introduction to MARPOL.answer: They show the garbage disposal requirements.

CD0092 — Introduction to MARPOL.question: Which one of the following best describes the requirement in MARPOL Annex VI intended to minimise accidental emissions from incinerators?
options: The operator is to be trained and have an operating manual
The incinerator is to have an annual service
The incinerator is to be supplied with an operating manual
The operator is to have been on the manufacturer’s training course
Incorrect
Correct
CD0092 — Introduction to MARPOL.answer: The operator is to be trained and have an operating manual

CD0092 — Introduction to MARPOL.question: Which one of the following options best describes how MARPOL Annex I controls the amount of oil discharged into the sea from the cargo tank areas of oil tankers?
options: The rate of discharge of oil is limited
Permits must be bought to allow oil to be discharged
No oil can be discharged into the sea from cargo tank areas
There is a fixed limit on the total amount of oil discharged per year
Incorrect
Correct
CD0092 — Introduction to MARPOL.answer: The rate of discharge of oil is limited

CD0092 — Introduction to MARPOL.question: Which one of the following most closely matches the definition of ‘sewage’ in MARPOL Annex IV?
options: Drainage from animals, medical premises, toilets and urinals
Drainage from sinks, baths and toilets and urinals
Solids from toilets
Grey water
Incorrect
Correct
CD0092 — Introduction to MARPOL.answer: Drainage from animals, medical premises, toilets and urinals

CD0092 — Introduction to MARPOL.question: Which one of the given options best explains why MARPOL Annex I requires most new tankers to be built with double hulls?
options: To reduce the chances of oil leaking into the sea following collision or grounding
To ensure that ships have enough ballast capacity to cope with storms
To reduce instability caused by the free surface effect on cargo
To increase port fees from tankers
Incorrect
Correct
CD0092 — Introduction to MARPOL.answer: To reduce the chances of oil leaking into the sea following collision or grounding

CD0092 — Introduction to MARPOL.question: Which one of the following is the main goal of MARPOL Annex I?
options: To reduce the harm to the environment from oil pollution from ships
To minimise the harm to seafarers from oil on ships
To reduce the harm to the environment from sewage pollution from ships
To minimise the number of oil tanker voyages
Incorrect
Correct
CD0092 — Introduction to MARPOL.answer: To reduce the harm to the environment from oil pollution from ships

CD0092 — Introduction to MARPOL.question: Which one of the following best describes what MARPOL Annex II requires to minimise the amount of noxious liquids when cleaning cargo tanks?
options: Tanks have to be stripped down to small volumes of cargo
Tanks have to be washed with the minimum of water
Tanks are not allowed to be washed with water
Tanks have to be emptied using ventilation fans
Incorrect
Correct
CD0092 — Introduction to MARPOL.answer: Tanks have to be stripped down to small volumes of cargo

CD0092 — Introduction to MARPOL.question: Which one of the following best describes the purpose of the garbage management plan that MARPOL Annex V requires some ships to carry?
options: It gives instructions for the collection, processing and storage of garbage before its disposal
It gives instructions for the disposal of garbage at sea only
It only gives instructions for garbage recycling
It only gives the actions to be taken following accidental discharge of garbage
Incorrect
Correct
CD0092 — Introduction to MARPOL.answer: It gives instructions for the collection, processing and storage of garbage before its disposal

CD0092 — Introduction to MARPOL.question: Which one of the following best describes the main goal of MARPOL Annex V?
options: To reduce the harm to the environment from garbage from ships
To ban the discharge of garbage into the sea
To ban discharges containing harmful substances
To reduce the harm to the environment from sewage from ships
Incorrect
Correct
CD0092 — Introduction to MARPOL.answer: To reduce the harm to the environment from garbage from ships

CD0092 — Introduction to MARPOL.question: Some MARPOL annexes require ships to be surveyed and certificated. Which one of the following is the most likely reason for this?
options: Compliance with some MARPOL rules cannot easily be proven while the ship is in service
It produces fees for class societies
It allows IMO to count the number of compliant ships
It is an excuse for flag states to visit their ships
Incorrect
Correct
CD0092 — Introduction to MARPOL.answer: Compliance with some MARPOL rules cannot easily be proven while the ship is in service

CD0092 — Introduction to MARPOL.question: Which one of the following best describes the main goal of MARPOL Annex IV?
options: To reduce the harm to the environment from sewage from ships
To reduce the amount of sewage produced by ships
To ensure that all sewage on ships is treated to break it down
To minimise the harm to the environment after an accidental discharge of sewage
Incorrect
Correct
CD0092 — Introduction to MARPOL.answer: To reduce the harm to the environment from sewage from ships

CD0092 — Introduction to MARPOL.question: A ship has sewage stored in a tank. Which one of the following best describes the MARPOL Annex IV requirements that must be met before the ship is allowed to discharge the tank contents overboard?
options: The ship must be away from land and pump the sewage at a controlled rate
The ship must be outside port limits
The ship must be away from land and moving at a minimum of 12 knots
The ship must be outside port limits and pump the sewage at a controlled rate
Incorrect
Correct
CD0092 — Introduction to MARPOL.answer: The ship must be away from land and pump the sewage at a controlled rate

CD0092 — Introduction to MARPOL.question: Which one of the following best describes how MARPOL Annex III attempts to reduce accidental loss of harmful substances in packaged form into the sea?
options: Packages are required to be properly stowed and secured
Packages are required to be made of durable plastic
Packages are required to be stowed below deck only
Packages are required to be inside a shipping container
Incorrect
Correct
CD0092 — Introduction to MARPOL.answer: Packages are required to be properly stowed and secured

CD0092 — Introduction to MARPOL.question: Which one of the following explains why MARPOL Annex I requires ships to have a sludge tank?
options: It is required to hold oil separated off by the bilge separator, sludge from purifiers and other waste oil
It is required only when ships have oil purifiers
It is only required to store bilge water until it can be discharged overboard
It is only required to hold the oil separated off by the bilge separator
Incorrect
Correct
CD0092 — Introduction to MARPOL.answer: It is required to hold oil separated off by the bilge separator, sludge from purifiers and other waste oil

CD0092 — Introduction to MARPOL.question: Which one of the following best describes how MARPOL Annex I reduces the amount of oil in ballast water discharges from oil tankers?
options: Ballast water is normally kept segregated from the cargo tanks
Tankers are designed not to need water ballast
Ballast water must be discharged via the slop tank
Ballast water is kept in fore and aft peak tanks only
Incorrect
Correct
CD0092 — Introduction to MARPOL.answer: Ballast water is normally kept segregated from the cargo tanks

CD0092 — Introduction to MARPOL.question: Which one of the following best describes how MARPOL Annex VI is intended to reduce leakages of Ozone Depleting Substances (ODS)?
options: By requiring an ozone depleting substance record book
By banning some of the ozone depleting substances from 2012
By increasing the cost of ozone depleting substances
By requiring a SOx Emissions Compliance Plan
Incorrect
Correct
CD0092 — Introduction to MARPOL.answer: By requiring an ozone depleting substance record book

CD0092 — Introduction to MARPOL.question: Which one of the following best describes the requirement in MARPOL Annex VI intended to minimise operational emissions of Sulphur Oxides (SOx)?
options: The sulphur content of fuel is limited
New diesel engines have to meet Tier II SOx limits
Sulphur scrubbers are required on all new engines
Bunker samples must be taken and kept ashore
Incorrect
Correct
CD0092 — Introduction to MARPOL.answer: The sulphur content of fuel is limited

CD0093 — Wall Wash.question: The significant difference with a Whatman Filter Paper test is that it:
options: Commonly includes a sample taken from the tank bottom.
Involves more samples per tank.
It is more difficult to pass.
It is only performed in Japan.
CD0093 — Wall Wash.answer: Commonly includes a sample taken from the tank bottom.

CD0093 — Wall Wash.question: Under normal handling conditions, a Permanganate Solution will last for approximately:
options: 1 year.
1 month.
Indefinitely.
3-5 days.

CD0093 — Wall Wash.question: Inhibitor in a previous cargo commonly affects Permanganate Fade Time test results  (True or False):
options: True.
False.

CD0093 — Wall Wash.question: Soapy bubbles noted on the top of a wall wash sample in a test tube are a likely indication of:
options: Residues from an oil based cleaning agent.
Residues of a water based cargo.
Residues from a detergent based cleaning chemical.
Acetone.
CD0093 — Wall Wash.answer: Residues from a detergent based cleaning chemical.

CD0093 — Wall Wash.question: In a Hydrocarbons test, the presence of slight Hydrocarbons is indicated by:
options: A milky white discoloration.
A silver sheen on the surface of the sample.
A translucent bluish tint.
A pale yellow haze.

5 drops of 10% Silver Nitrate Solution.

5 ml of 3% Hydrochloric Acid.

CD0093 — Wall Wash.question: A drying-oven Non-Volatile Matter test cannot be effectively done on board a ship because:
options: The equipment works on a different voltage.
Spares are difficult to obtain in many parts of the world.
A sufficiently stable and vibration-free platform cannot be provided for the required measurements.
Ship’s laboratories cannot be maintained at constant room temperature.
CD0093 — Wall Wash.answer: A sufficiently stable and vibration-free platform cannot be provided for the required measurements.

CD0093 — Wall Wash.question: In a Permanganate Fade Time test, how long should the samples be allowed to “stabilise” before the Permanganate solution is added?
options: At least 10 minutes.
Maximum 30 minutes.
2 minutes.
Approx 45 minutes.

CD0093 — Wall Wash.question: The ratio and components used in the preparation of a Permanganate Solution are:

0.1g Permanganate crystals to 0.5 ltr Methanol.
0.1g Permanganate crystals to 0.5 ltr Deionised Water.

CD0093 — Wall Wash.question: The Ultra-Violet Spectrum test is run to detect:
options: Acid.
Hydrocarbons.
High levels of solid particle impurities.
Low levels of dissolved impurities.

CD0093 — Wall Wash.question: The most likely source of Hydrocarbons detected in a wall wash sample is:
options: Dust in the laboratory Methanol.
Polluted air drawn into the tank.
Traces of previous cargo.
Equipment failure.

Methanol will turn the marker ink sticky and it may get transferred to the wall wash funnel.
Under the regulations, coloured marker pens are prohibited.

CD0093 — Wall Wash.question: The following important information should be prominently posted in the ship’s laboratory:

Material Safety Data Sheets for any chemicals in use.
Cleaning Chemical Index.

CD0093 — Wall Wash.question: Of the four problems listed below and assuming all are included in a customer specification, which would be the priority?

Moderate Hydrocarbons.
Heavy Chlorides.
Very slight Odour.

CD0093 — Wall Wash.question: The purpose of a wall wash is to determine:
options: Whether a tank meets customer cleanliness requirements.
If a tank is dry.
Whether a tank meets company maintenance requirements.
If a tank is safe to enter.
CD0093 — Wall Wash.answer: Whether a tank meets customer cleanliness requirements.

CD0093 — Wall Wash.question: Maintaining the samples at a constant temperature is a necessary part of the Permanganate Fade Time test procedure. True or False?:

False.

CD0093 — Wall Wash.question: In a Permanganate Fade Time test using Methanol, at what temperature should the samples be maintained?

CD0093 — Wall Wash.question: The two components in a Hydrocarbon test “blank” standard are:

Methanol and Silver Nitrate Solution.

CD0093 — Wall Wash.question: Where possible, a wall wash stream should be run for:

Minimum 1 metre.
2 metres.

A Potassium Cobalt 530 colour standard.
An API 500 Colour standard.

CD0093 — Wall Wash.question: The dish used in a shore laboratory Non-Volatile Matter test is commonly made from:

Stainless steel.
Platinum.
Teflon coated metal.

CD0093 — Wall Wash.question: A wall wash should not be taken from a wet bulkhead because:

CD0093 — Wall Wash.question: To assess the Appearance of a wall wash sample, we:

A wall wash should not be taken from a hot bulkhead because:

CD0093 — Wall Wash.question: In a Permanganate Fade Time test, samples should be checked against the standard at the following interval:

Continuously.

General Chromatography.

Gas Chromatography.

CD0093 — Wall Wash.question: The over-riding principle behind a wall wash and the subsequent analysis is:

Agreement between the Chief Officer and the Surveyor.

CD0093 — Wall Wash.question: If you encounter a new wall wash or analysis procedure, you should:

Advise the Ship’s Superintendent.
Ignore it.

CD0093 — Wall Wash.question: The wall wash procedures in this programme, and those used by the majority of shore laboratories, are built around industry standards issued by the following organisation:
options: The American Society for Testing and Materials.
The American Petroleum Institute.
System International.

CD0096 — Cargo Compatibility.question: A “Safe Stowage” is one in which:
options: Hazardously reactive cargoes will not be stowed in wing tanks.
There will always be a cofferdam between tanks which contain hazardously reactive cargoes.
Hazardously reactive cargoes will not be stowed in compartments with a common boundary.
Incompatible cargoes will be stowed in adjacent compartments.
CD0096 — Cargo Compatibility.answer: Hazardously reactive cargoes will not be stowed in compartments with a common boundary.

CD0096 — Cargo Compatibility.question: In respect of the Compatibility Chart, a “Hazardous Reaction” is defined as one in which mixing of the products results in:
options: A breakdown of the common boundary between the two tanks.
A rise in temperature of more than 10°C, or from which a gas is evolved.
A rise in temperature of more than 25°C, or from which a gas is evolved.
A chemical reaction in the tank with the greater ullage.
CD0096 — Cargo Compatibility.answer: A rise in temperature of more than 25°C, or from which a gas is evolved.
